1Ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne aso Mose tole ye sa frɛle Aarɔn ne ye mma mmienzua nemɔ ɔne Yisrael mbanyi; 2na osele Aarɔn kyɛ, “Fa nandwie nyii akrɔngrɔma bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ma AWURADE, ná fa boaen nyii bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ma AWURADE. Onni kyɛ ngaka ne anu biala yɛ bɔ wali nnɛen ɔ. 3Na ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, ‘Ɛ́mɔfa abɔngye nyii bɛ́bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ, ná ɛ́mɔfa nandwie akrɔngrɔma ne boaen akrɔngrɔma bɔ bali afoɛ ngoko ngoko, bɔ bellili nnɛen biala ɔ bɛ́bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ. 4Ɛ́mɔfa nandwie nyii ne boaen nyii, ɔne aburoo afɔleɛ bɔ bafa ngoo bafra ye ɔ bɛbɔ asomdwee afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu; ofikyɛ ɛnɛ Nyameɛ kɔye ye nwo ali kohyire ɛmɔ.’ ” 5Bɛfale bɔ Mose hyɛle bɛ ne bɛwale ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anyunu berɛ, na Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa bɔ pingyele beegyinane AWURADE nyunu. 6Na Mose sele kyɛ, “Nikyee bɔ AWURADE hyɛle ɛmɔ kyɛ ɛmɔyɔ ɛhe, amaa ɔnate so AWURADE aye ye animnyam ali wahyire ɛmɔ.” 7Yeɛ Mose sele Aarɔn kyɛ, “Twe pingye afɔleɛ bokyea ne, ná bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ɔne naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ma wɔ nwo, ná yɛ mbata ma wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ nwo ne wɔ mmenia ne; ná fa mmenia nemɔ afɔleɛ nningyein ne bra baapata ma bɛ, kyɛbɔ AWURADE ahyɛ ne.”
8Aarɔn pingyele afɔleɛ bokyea ne, na ohuni nandwie bɔ ɔfa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ mane ye nwo ne. 9Aarɔn mma mmienzua nemɔ fale mogya ne bɛbrɛle ye. Ɔfale ye sa mmɛseka bɔle mogya ne anu fa yɛle afɔleɛ bokyea ne mmɛen nemɔ anwo, na mogya bɔ waha ne, ohwiele guale afɔleɛ bokyea ne abo. 10Nakoso bɔne nwo afɔleɛ loe ne, ye saa nemɔ, ɔne ye boɛ ne bie de, ɔyerale bɛ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso, kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle Mose ne. 11Na ye naen ne ye nwomaa ne de, ɔfale see yerale bɛ wɔ asikyeleɛ ne asi.
12Afei Aarɔn huni naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ kaka ne, na ye mma mmienzua nemɔ fale kaka ne mogya ne bɛbrɛle ye, na ohwie guale afɔleɛ bokyea ne anwo bra yiale. 13Na bɛfale naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne naenguma naenguma ɔne ye ti ne bɛbrɛle ye; na ɔyerale bɛ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso. 14Onwunzini ye kunu nningyein ne ɔne ye gya nemɔ anwo, na ɔfa bokale naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne aso ɔyerale bɛ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso.
15Ye si ye, ɔfale maen afɔleɛ ne wale. Ɔfale maen bɔne nwo afɔleɛ abɔngye ne. Ohuni ye, na ɔfa bɔle bɔne nwo afɔleɛ kyɛbɔ ɔyɔle bɔ oli moa ne ala. 16Ɔfale naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne wale, na ɔbɔle afɔleɛ ne kyɛbɔ nhyehyɛleɛ ne te ne. 17Ɔfale aburoo afɔleɛ ne wale. Ɔsale ye sa bum ko, ɔfa bokale ngyerɛmɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne aso, na ɔyerale bɛ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso.
18 Aarɔn huni nandwie nyii ne ɔne boaen nyii ne fa bɔle asomdwee afɔleɛ mane maen ne; na ye mma nemɔ fale mogya ne bɛbrɛle ye, maa ohwie guale afɔleɛ bokyea ne anwo bra yiale. 19Bɛfale ɛhemɔ koso bɛbrɛle ye: nandwie nyii loe ne ɔne boaen nyii loe ne, bɛ dua pue ne, ɛloe bɔ wato wafa bɛ kunu nningyein ne anwo ne, bɛ saa nyɔ ne, ɔne ye bɛ boɛ ne bie. 20Belili moa bɛfale ɛloe ne beguale ye sa nemɔ aso, na ɔyerale ɛloe ne wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso. 21Nakoso ye sa nemɔ ne ye sɔ famaa ne de, Aarɔn pagyale fa bɔle ɛnwahanɛ afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu kyɛbɔ Mose hyɛle ne.
22 Aarɔn mane ye sa so fa hyirele mmenia ne aso, na oyirale bɛ. Ɔbɔle bɔne nwo afɔleɛ, naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ɔne asomdwee afɔleɛ yiele nen, odwu wale ase. 23Mose ne Aarɔn wurale ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anu. Afei befi berɛ befitele beeyirayirale mmenia ne, na AWURADE yele ye animnyam ali hyirele mmenia ne amukoraa. 24See fili AWURADE berɛ ɔɔyerale naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne, ɔne ɛloe bɔ ɔwɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso ne. Mmerɛ bɔ mmenia ne amu benwuni ye ne, bɛteateane nu, na bɛfale bɛ nyunu bebutubutuli ase.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Nadabo ne Abihu yɔ bɔne
1Aarɔn mma mmienzua Nadabo ne Abihu, bɛ nu biala fale ye see kulie. Bɛfale see beguale nu, na bɛfale ɛyɛɛ beguale so. Bɛfale see bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ bɛwale AWURADE nyunu, see bɔ nna AWURADE yeɛ wahyɛ bɛ kyɛ bɛfa bɛbra ye nyunu ɔ. 2See fili AWURADE berɛ ɔɔyerale bɛ ná bɛtotɔle wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 3Na Mose sele Aarɔn kyɛ, “Bɔ AWURADE aha hɔ ɛhe:
‘Ɔnate bɛ bɔ bepingye me ne aso,
ngɔmaa bekonwu me kyɛ nde krongron,
na bɛkɔhyɛ me animnyam
wɔ mmenia ne amukoraati nyunu.’ ”
Na Aarɔn yɛle konn.
4Mose tole ye sa frɛle Aarɔn ɔse aliɛma Yusiɛl ye mma mmienzua Misael ne Ɛlsafan, na osele bɛ kyɛ, “Ɛ́mɔpingye wa ná ɛmɔsoa ɛmɔ aliɛma nemɔ béfi nekaa krongron ne anyunu berɛ bɛhɔ asikyeleɛ ne asi dɔ.” 5Yiti kyɛbɔ Mose hyɛle ne, bepingyele berɛ na bɛsoale bɛ fuin nemɔ wɔ b’aguasoɛ nu befili asikyeleɛ ne anu. 6Na Mose sele Aarɔn, ɔne Aarɔn mma mmienzua Eleasa ne Yitama kyɛ, “Nnɛmɔma ɛmɔ ti nwiaa fu gua ye nwo fusaa, yeɛ nnɛma ɛmɔsunzua ɛmɔ ndaadeɛ nu. Sɛ ɔba ye sɔ a, ɛmɔkowu, na AWURADE ɛyaafɛlɛ piri kɔwa maen ne amukoraa so. Nakoso ɛmɔ aliɛma mɔ, Yisrael awuro ama mukoraa de, bɛkɔhora bekosu bɛ bɔ AWURADE afa see wayera bɛ ne. 7Nnɛma ɛmɔfi ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anoa nu berɛ bɛkɔ, anyɔ a ɛmɔkowu, ofikyɛ AWURADE afa ɛpopalɛ ngoo wapopa ɛmɔ.” Na bɛyɔle kyɛbɔ Mose hyɛle ne ala.
8 AWURADE sele Aarɔn kyɛ, 9“Ɛne wɔ mma mmienzua mɔ, sɛ ɛmɔkɔ ɛtena sua ne anu a, nnɛma ɛmɔno bobe nzaa anaa nzaa serɛ biala amaa ɛmɔanwu; ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔyɛ ahyɛdeɛ afebɔɔ wɔ ɛmɔ aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ amukoraa nu. 10Odi kyɛ ɛmɔnwu nzonzoleɛ bɔ ɔla nikyee bɔ ɔte krongron ɔne nikyee bɔ ɔtte krongron b’afia, nzonzoleɛ bɔ ɔla nikyee bɔ ye nwo nde ɔne bɔ ye nwo te ɔ b’afia; 11na odi kyɛ ɛmɔkyirekyire Yisraelfoɛ ahyɛdeɛ bɔ AWURADE nate Mose so ha hyirele bɛ ne amukoraa.”
12 Mose sele Aarɔn ɔne Aarɔn mma bɔ baha bɔ bɛ ole Eleasa ne Yitama kyɛ, “Afɔleɛ mɔ bɔ bɛbɔle ye see so bɛmane AWURADE ne, ɛ́mɔfa aburoo afɔleɛ ngaa ne, ná ɛ́mɔli ye kabrɛdi wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne ngyɛnu, ofikyɛ ɔte krongron paa. 13Odi kyɛ ɛmɔdi ye wɔ nekaa bɔ ɔte krongron ɔ, ofikyɛ afɔleɛ bɔ babɔ ye see so bama AWURADE ne, ɛne wɔ mma mɔ bɛ deɛ ɛne; sɔ yeɛ AWURADE ahyehyɛ ama me ɔ. 14 Nakoso ye sa bɔ bɛnwaha ne, ɔne ye sɔ bɔ bɛfa bɛbɔle afɔleɛ ne, ɛ́mɔli ye wɔ nekaa bɔ berɛ te sannwuu ɔ. Ɛne wɔ mma mmienzua ne wɔ mma mmrasua mɔ yeɛ beli ɔ, ofikyɛ Yisraelfoɛ asomdwee afɔleɛ ne, ɛne wɔ mma mɔ, ɛmɔ deɛ bɔ ɔwɔ nu hɔ ɛne. 15Ye sɔ bɔ bɛfa bɛbɔ afɔleɛ ne, ɔne ye sa bɔ bɛnwaha ne de, odi kyɛ bɛfa bɛboka ɛloe bɔ bɛfa see bɛyera bɛbɔ afɔleɛ ne aso bɛba, ná bɛfa bɛbɔ ɛnwahanɛ afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu, na ɔkɔyɛ wɔ ne wɔ mma mɔ deɛ afebɔɔ, kyɛbɔ AWURADE ahyɛ ne.”
16Na bɔne nwo afɔleɛ abɔngye ne de, Mose penane ye fɛle, nakoso né bayera ye dada. Yiti ɔfɛle Eleasa ne Yitama, bɔ bɛ ole Aarɔn mma mmienzua bɔ baha ne bɛ so yaa, na obisale kyɛ, 17 “Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔanni bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ne wɔ nekaa bɔ ɔte krongron ɔ? Ofikyɛ ɔte nikye krongron paa, na Nyameɛ afa ama ɛmɔ, amaa ɛmɔaprapra mmenia nemɔ amumuyɛɛ bagua na ɛmɔapata bama bɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 18Ɛ́mɔnea, ɛmɔamva ye mogya ne bamma nekaa krongron ne anu. Ahaa odi kyɛ ɛmɔdi ye wɔ nekaa krongron ne anu berɛ, kyɛbɔ nhyɛle ɛmɔ ne.” 19Na Aarɔn sele Mose kyɛ, “Tie, ɛnɛ bafa bɛ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ne bɛ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ bawa Nyameɛ nyunu, yeɛ koso edwirɛ hemɔ ato me ye! Aso sɛ nnili bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ye ɛnɛ a, ahaa AWURADE nye kɔsɔ anaa?” 20Na Mose tele sɔ nen, ye ahone tɔle ye kunu.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_text:
Aleɛ bɔ ye nwo te ɔne bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ
(Deuteronomi 14.3-21)
1AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, 2 “Ɛ́mɔhã behyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, ‘Aseɛ ye aso ngaka amukoraa, bɛ nu horɛ bɔ ɛ́mɔli ɛhe: 3Kaka biala bɔ ye gya ne anu apakye, bɔ ye gya ne wura mbaboa, ná opu ye aleɛ sá pesa ne, ɛmɔkɔhora bekoli. 4Nakoso bɛbɔ bepu b’aleɛ besa bɛpesa anaa bɛ gya ne anu apakye ne, nnɛma ɛmɔdi ɛhemɔ: afupɔngɔ, ofikyɛ ɔwɔ nu kyɛ opu ye aleɛ sá pesa de, nakoso ye gya ne anu de ɔppakyele, yiti ye nwo nde mma ɛmɔ, 5ɔne akrande, ofikyɛ ɔwɔ nu kyɛ opu ye aleɛ osa pesa de, nakoso ye gya ne anu de ɔppakyele, yiti ye nwo nde mma ɛmɔ; 6yeɛ adango, ofikyɛ ɔwɔ nu kyɛ opu ye aleɛ osa pesa de, nakoso ye gya ne anu de ɔppakyele, yiti ye nwo nde mma ɛmɔ; 7ɔne prako, ofikyɛ ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ye gya ne anu apakye, bɔ ye gya ne wura mbaboa de, nakoso ombu ye aleɛ mbesa, yiti ye nwo nde mma ɛmɔ. 8Nnɛma ɛmɔdi bɛ naen, yeɛ bɛ fuin koso nnɛma ɛmɔsɔ nu; bɛ nwo nde mma ɛmɔ.
9“Nzue nu naen mɔ koso, ɛhemɔ yeɛ ɛ́mɔli ɔ: kaka biala bɔ ɔwɔ nzue nu, bɔ ole ndɛtɛ ne ɛboen ne, kyɛ ɔwɔ ɛpo nu oo, anaa asue nu oo, ɛmɔkɔhora bekoli. 10Nakoso nzue nu ngaka worawora ɔne nzue nu ngaka bɔ bele ngoa de, bɛ nu biala bɔ olle ndɛtɛ ɔne ɛboen ne, kyɛ ɔwɔ ɛpo nu oo, kyɛ ɔwɔ asue nu oo, ɔte akyiwadeɛ ma ɛmɔ. 11Bɛkɔhɔ so bɛkɔyɛ akyiwadeɛ; nnɛma ɛmɔdi bɛ naen, ná bɛ fuin koso ɛ́mɔbu ye akyiwadeɛ. 12Nzue nu kaka biala bɔ olle ndɛtɛ ɔne ɛboen ne, ɔte akyiwadeɛ ma ɛmɔ.
13“Nnomaa mɔ nu koso ɛhemɔ kɔyɛ ɛmɔ akyiwadeɛ; onni kyɛ bedi ɔ, bɛte akyiwadeɛ: kɔleɛ, pɛtɛ, akorɔma, 14akompɛtɛ, senza ahoroɔ, 15adene ahoroɔ amukoraati, 16soholi, kɔngɔen akorɔma, ɛpo so dabodabo, akorɔma ahoroɔ, 17patue, nandwinoma, patue mbiri, 18asudabo, ɛserɛ so patue, pɛtɛ fufue, 19akyemvona katakyie, asunoma ahoroɔ, asuakwaa ne apena.
20“Kaka biala bɔ ole ndaa, ná ɔnate ye gya nna so ne, ɔte akyiwadeɛ ma ɛmɔ. 21Nakoso ngaka bɔ bele ndaa ná bɛfa bɛ gya nna amukoraa bɛnate, ná bele agyirɛ wɔ nziɛ bɔ bɛfa behuru fɛen fɛen wɔ aseɛ so ne, 22bɛ nu ɛhemɔ yeɛ ɛ́mɔli ɔ: mmɛbɛ ahoroɔ, mmɛbɛ mbiri ahoroɔ, ngetekyire ahoroɔ, yeɛ torɔka ahoroɔ. 23Nakoso ngaka ngaa bɔ bele ndaa ná bele agyirɛ nna ne de, bɛte ɛmɔ akyiwadeɛ.
24“Ɛhemɔ yeɛ ɔma ɛmɔ nwo gua fiɛ ɔ: ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha bɛ fuin ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa, 25na ebiala bɔ ɔkɔsoa bɛ nu biala fuin nen, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, na ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okodwu nɔsoa. 26Kaka biala bɔ ye gya ne anu apakye nakoso ye gya ne owwura mbaboa, anaakyɛ ombu ye aleɛ mbesa ne, ye nwo nde mma ɛmɔ; sona biala bɔ ye nwo kɔha bɛ ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ. 27Na ngaka amukoraa bɔ bɛnate bɛ gya nna so ne, bɛ nu biala bɔ ɔnate ye gya tasaa nu ne, ye nwo nde mma ɛmɔ; ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha bɛ fuin ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 28Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔsoa bɛ fuin ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, na ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa; bɛ nwo nde mma ɛmɔ.
29“Ngaka bɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo ase ne, ɛhemɔ yeɛ bɛ nwo nde mma ɛmɔ ɔ: abotokura, mmurokuruwa, benze ahoroɔ, 30ɛlaleɛ, benze, epo, bɔmɔtebɔmɔ ɔne dodowurowuro. 31Bɛ bɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo ase ne, ɛhemɔ bɛ nwo nde mma ɛmɔ. Sɛ bewu a, ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha bɛ fuin ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 32Nikyee biala bɔ bɛ nu biala fuin kɔtɔ so ne, kyɛ bakaa yeɛ bafa bayɔ hɔ oo, anaa ɛtena oo, anaa nwomaa oo, anaa bɔtɔ oo, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bɛfa bɛyɔ adwuma biala oo, odi kyɛ bɛfa bewura nzue nu na ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa koraka ne ye nwo ate. 33Kukue biala bɔ bɛ nu biala kɔte kɔtɔ nu ne, nikyee biala bɔ ɔwɔ sɔ kukue ne anu nwo kogua fiɛ na odi kyɛ ɛmɔbɔ kukue ne. 34Aleɛ biala bɔ odi kyɛ bedi nakoso sɔ kukue ne anu nzue kogua so ne, ye nwo agua fiɛ, na anonneɛ biala bɔ bɛno nakoso ofi sɔ kukue ne anu ne, ye nwo agua fiɛ. 35Nikyee biala bɔ bɛ nu biala fuin ye nekaa biala kɔtɔ so ne, kyɛ ɔte foonoo oo, anaa bokyea oo, odi kyɛ bebubu ye begua; ye nwo nde, na odi kyɛ ɛmɔbu ye kyɛ ye nwo nde. 36Mbombonzue anaa abura nu nzue nwo te; nakoso sɛ nikyee bie la nu, ná sɔ ngaka nemɔ nu bie fuin ka ye a, sɔ nikyee ne nwo nde. 37Sɛ bɛ fuin ne, ye nekaa biala te tɔ mmakaammaa bɔ bɛkwaalua so a, mmakaammaa ne nwo te; 38nakoso sɛ bɛfa mmakaammaa ne begua nzue nu, na sɛ kaka ne fuin ne nekaa biala te tɔ so a, mmakaammaa ne nwo nde mma ɛmɔ.
39“Kaka biala bɔ ɛmɔle ate kyɛ bedi ne, sɛ owu a, sona biala bɔ ye nwo kɔha ye fuin ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 40Sona biala bɔ okoli ye naenmvuin ne bie ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, na ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okodwu nɔsoa; sona bɔ ɔkɔsoa kaka fuin ne koso, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein na ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa.
41“Kaka biala bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ne ase, ɔte akyiwadeɛ; onni kyɛ ɛmɔdi ɔ. 42Kaka biala bɔ ɔnate ye ko so, ɔne kaka biala bɔ ɔnate ye gya nna so, anaa kaka biala bɔ ole agyirɛ pee, ɔne ngaka biala bɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo ase ne, nnɛma ɛmɔdi; ofikyɛ bɛte akyiwadeɛ. 43Nnɛma ɛmɔfa kaka biala bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ase begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ, nnɛma ɛmɔfa bɛ begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ amaa ɛmɔanyɛ mmenia bɔ bɛ nwo nde ɔ. 44 Ofikyɛ me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ; yiti ɛ́mɔte ɛmɔ anwo, ná ɛ́mɔyɛ krongron ofikyɛ nde krongron. Nnɛma ɛmɔfa kaka biala bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ase begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ. 45Ofikyɛ me ole AWURADE bɔ nyele ɛmɔ mvili Misraim aseɛ so mmale ne, bɔ me yeɛ nde ɛmɔ Nyameɛ ɔ; yiti ɛ́mɔyɛ krongron, ofikyɛ nde krongron.”
46 Ɛhe ole mmeraa bɔ ɔfa aseɛnwo ngaka, nnomaa, nzue nu kaka biala bɔ ole ngoa ɔne kaka biala bɔ ɔtwe ye nwo ase nwo ɔ, 47kyɛ ɛmɔkɔma nzonzoleɛ kɔla nningyein bɔ bɛ nwo te ɔne bɛbɔ bɛ nwo nde afia; ngaka bɔ odi kyɛ ɛmɔdi ɔne bɔ onni kyɛ ɛmɔdi ɔ afia.

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Aworɛ si anwopetenɛ
1 Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, 2“Ka kyire Yisrael ama kyɛ sɛ brasua ɔnwonzɛ, ná ɔwo bienzua a, ye nwo kogua fiɛ alaa ɛlɛsoo, ye nwo kogua fiɛ kyɛ mmerɛ bɔ wabu ye sa ne ala. 3 Na ye ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne aso, odi kyɛ bɛpɛ akwadaa ne bienzua. 4Braa ne koli ngyẽa eleburasa ne nza koraka né ye nwo ate afi mogya bɔ wagua ye ne anwo; onni kyɛ ɔfa ye nwo ka nikyee biala bɔ ɔte krongron ɔ, anaa ɔkɔ nekaa krongron ne anu kɔpem kyẽa bɔ ɔkɔpete ye nwo ne koyie ɔ. 5Nakoso sɛ ɔwo brasua de a, ye de ye nwo kogua fiɛ dapɛn nyɔ, kyɛ wabu ye sa ne ala, na braa ne koli ngyẽa eleburasia ne nzia koraka né ye nwo ate wafi mogya bɔ wagua ye ne anwo.
6“Na ngyẽa bɔ braa ne ɔfa pete ye nwo ne yie a, kyɛ baa bienzua deɛ oo, anaa baa brasua deɛ oo, odi kyɛ ɔfa ɛhemɔ brɛ ɔsɔfo ne wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne nyunu berɛ: boaen akrɔngrɔma bɔ wali afoɛ ko bɔ ɔbaafa bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ, ɔne aborɔnoma buruwa ko anaa aborɔma ko bɔ ɔbaafa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ɔ. 7Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa bɔ afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu, ná ɔ́fa yɛ mbata ma braa ne. Afei braa ne nwo kɔte kofi mogya bɔ wagua ye ne anwo. Mmeraa he wɔ berɛ ma brasua biala bɔ ɔkɔwo baa bienzua anaakyɛ baa brasua ɔ. 8 Na sɛ braa ne nwo ngɔso boaen so a, ye de ɔ́fa mmubure nyɔ anaa mmorɔnoma buruwa nyɔ ɔ́bra; ko te naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ, yeɛ ko wora te bɔne nwo afɔleɛ; odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa yɛ mbata ma braa ne ma ye nwo fi.”

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
Anwoɔnaen anwonyerɛ nwo mmeraa
1AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, 2“Sɛ asee gua ebie anwo, anaa edoee yɛ ye, anaa yira bobɔ ye ná ɔkakyi kwata wɔ ye nwo a, odi kyɛ bɛfa ye bɛbrɛ ɔsɔfo Aarɔn anaa Aarɔn mma mmienzua bɔ bɛte asɔfo nemɔ anu ko. 3Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea nekaa bɔ anwonyerɛ ne agua ye ne; na sɛ berɛ nwiaa ne ayɛ hoyaa, ná berɛ ne adidi ahɔ nu atra ye nwonaen ngaa ne a, ye de né ɔte kwata anwonyerɛ; sɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo yie a, odi kyɛ ɔfa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ne nwo nde. 4Na sɛ ye nwonaen ne berɛ te hoyaa, nakoso wannidi wangɔ nu wandra ye nwonaen ngaa ne, ná berɛ nwiaa ne wanyɛ hoyaa a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ma yarefoɛ ne ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo. 5Ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo, ná sɛ onwu kyɛ anwonyerɛ ne ɔtɛte kyɛbɔ ɔte ne ala, ná wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ma ye ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo bieku. 6Ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne osa neanea ye nwo, ná sɛ anwonyerɛ ne noa abrɛ ase bɔ wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ne ye nwo te; edoee mbaen ɔ; odi kyɛ sɔ sona ne, ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ye nwo ɔte. 7Nakoso, sɛ ɔfa ye nwo kokyire ɔsɔfo maa ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo afi, ná ye si ye sɛ edoee ne sa didi kɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ osa ba ɔsɔfo ne berɛ. 8Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo, na sɛ anwonyerɛ ne adidi ahɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo nde; kwata anwonyerɛ ɔ.
9“Sɛ kwata anwonyerɛ yɛ ebie a, odi kyɛ bɛfa ye bɛbrɛ ɔsɔfo ne. 10Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea yarefoɛ ne anwo, na sɛ mbɔmbɔ fufue bie anwu ye maa ye nwiaa ne ayɛ hoyaa, ná naen monɛ bie aworɔ tua mbɔmbɔ ne anu a, 11ye de né kwata koangɔ yeɛ wayɛ ye nwonaen ne. Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ne ye nwo nde. Ɔnzɛ kyɛ ɔma ye ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie, ofikyɛ sɔ sona ne ye nwo nde. 12Na sɛ kwata anwonyerɛ ne ye ye nwo ali wɔ ye wereɛ nu, maa kwata anwonyerɛ ne to pete yarefoɛ ne nwo fi ye ti so kɔpem ye gya bo, bɔ ɔsɔfo ne nye tua a, 13ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo, ná sɛ anwonyerɛ ne ayɛ sona ne nwo amukoraa a, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo te; ɔnate kyɛ ye nwo amu aturu hyɛnn, ná ye nwo te. 14Nakoso sɛ naen monɛ worɔ tua ye nwo a, ye de ye nwo nde. 15Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea naen monɛ ne, ná ɔfa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo nde. Naen monɛ ne nwo nde, ofikyɛ ɔte kwata anwonyerɛ. 16Nakoso sɛ naen monɛ ne sá kakyi yɛ fufue a, odi kyɛ sɔ sona ne ba ɔsɔfo ne berɛ. 17Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo, na sɛ anwonyerɛ ne ayɛ hoyaa a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ yarefoɛ ne, ye nwo te; ye nwo te.
18“Sɛ mbɔmbɔ kenamvoen wɔ ebie anwo, 19ná sɛ nikyee fufue bie anaa nikyee kɔkorɛ hoyaa bie nwu nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔfa kokyire ɔsɔfo ne. 20Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo, na sɛ onwu kyɛ wadidi wahɔ ye wereɛ nu ná ye nwiaa ayɛ hoyaa a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo nde; kwata anwonyerɛ ɛne, wala ali wɔ mbɔmbɔ ne anu. 21Nakoso sɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea, ná sɛ so nwiaa ne ɔyyɛle hoyaa, ná wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ ne anu, ná mmom sɛ anwonyerɛ ne aberɛ ase a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔma ye ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo. 22Na sɛ wadidi wɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sona ne, ye nwo nde; anwonyerɛ aha ye. 23Nakoso sɛ anwonyerɛ ne wɔ neka horɛ bɔ wandrɛ de a, ɔte mbɔmbɔ kenamvoen; odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo te.
24“Sɛ nikyee hyerɛ bie yera ebie ná ye berɛ wereɛ ne bɔ mvumvunya yɛ kɔkorɛ hoyaa anaa hyɛnn a, 25odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔnea, na sɛ berɛ nwiaa ne ayɛ hoyaa, ná wadidi wahɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de né kwata anwonyerɛ ɔ; wala ali wɔ mvumvunya ne anu. Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ne ye nwo nde; ɔte kwata anwonyerɛ. 26Nakoso sɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea, ná sɛ berɛ nwiaa ne wanyɛ hoyaa ná wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ nu, ná mmom wabrɛ ase a, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ma ye ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo. 27Ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ye nwo. Sɛ anwonyerɛ ne adidi ahɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ne ye nwo nde; ɔte kwata anwonyerɛ. 28Na sɛ anwonyerɛ ne wɔ nekaa horɛ ná wandrɛ wɔ ye wereɛ nu, ná mmom wabrɛ ase a, ye de nikyee hyerɛ yeɛ wama berɛ abɔ mvumvunya ɔ; odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔfa to dwaa kyɛ sona ne ye nwo te; ofikyɛ ɔte see kenamvoen.
29“Sɛ bienzua anaa brasua bie nya anwonyerɛ wɔ ye ti so anaa ye kanza nu a, 30odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea anwonyerɛ ne. Sɛ wadidi wahɔ ye wereɛ nu, ná sɛ berɛ nwiaa ne ayɛ hoyaa ndrɛko ndrɛko a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ye nwo nde; ɔte anwonyerɛ bɔ ɔyɛ kyee ɔ; ɔte kwata anwonyerɛ bɔ wayɛ ye ti so anaa ye kanza ɔ. 31Na sɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne, ná sɛ wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ nu, ná sɛ nwiaa tunn biala offuli nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔma sɔ sona bɔ anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ayɛ ye ne ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo. 32Ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne; ná sɛ anwonyerɛ ne wandrɛ, ná sɛ nwiaa hoyaa ɔnne nu, ná sɛ anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ nu a, 33ye de odi kyɛ ɔpoa ye nwo nwiaa, nakoso nnɛma ɔpoa anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne anu; odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔma sona bɔ anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ayɛ ye ne ngome ɔte ye nwo kɔtena nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo bieku. 34Ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ɔneanea anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne, ná sɛ anwonyerɛ ne wandrɛ wangɔ ye wereɛ nu ná wannidi wangɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ sɔ sona ne ye nwo te. Odi kyɛ sɔ sona ne po ye nwo nningyein, ná ye nwo kɔte. 35Nakoso sɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo te, ná ye si ye, anwonyerɛ ne trɛ wɔ ye wereɛ nu a, 36ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔneanea ye nwo, ná sɛ anwonyerɛ ne atrɛ wɔ ye wereɛ nu a, ye de ye nwo nhia kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne kɔpena nwiaa hoyaa ne ɔ; ye nwo nde. 37Na mmom sɛ ye adwene yɛ ye kyɛ anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne ɔtɛte kyɛbɔ ɔte ɔ, ná nwiaa tunn afu wɔ nu a, ye de ne anwonyerɛ kyeekyee ne ahɔ. Ye nwo te; odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo te.
38“Sɛ ndotɔndotɔ fufue bie gua bienzua anaa brasua bie nwo a, 39odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔneanea ye nwo, ná sɛ ndotɔndotɔ bɔ wagua ye ne te fufue hoyaa a, ye de asee yeɛ wagua ye nwo ɔ; ye nwo te.
40“Sɛ ebie ti so tutu a, ye ti so yeɛ wapa ɔ nakoso ye nwo te. 41Na sɛ ebie ye nwoma so pa ná ye ti angyɛnu tutu a, ye de ye nwoma so yeɛ wapa ɔ, nakoso ye nwo te. 42Nakoso sɛ anwonyerɛ kɔkorɛ hoyaa bie wɔ ye ti bɔ wapa ne aso, anaa ye nwoma bɔ wapa ne aso a, ye de né kwata yeɛ wayɛ ye ti bɔ wapa ne aso anaa ye nwoma bɔ wapa ne aso ɔ. 43Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea yarefoɛ ne anwo, ná sɛ nikyee bɔ wagua ye ti afia anaa ye nwoma bɔ wapa ne aso ne, ɔte kɔkorɛ hoyaa, bɔ osoma kwata anwonyerɛ wɔ ye wereɛ nu a, 44ye de né ɔte kwataniɛ. Ye nwo nde, na odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ ye nwo nde; ye anwonyerɛ ne wɔ ye ti so.
45“Sona bɔ kwata anwonyerɛ kɔyɛ ye ne, odi kyɛ owura ndaadeɛ teterewaa ná ɔma ye ti nwiaa gua so basaa. Odi kyɛ ɔkata ye noa tuin anwuro ne aso ná ɔtea nu kyɛ, ‘Me nwo nde o, me nwo nde o! 46Na mmerɛ bɔ anwonyerɛ ne tɛ wɔ ye so ne de, ye de ye nwo nde. Ye nwo nde na ye ngome ɔkɔte ye nwo kɔɔtena asikyeleɛ ne asi.
47“Sɛ kwata anwonyerɛ kekã ataadeɛ nu a, kyɛ kundu ahɔ oo, anaa nwera ahɔ oo, 48kundu anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo nu oo, anaa bɔ bafa boaen nwiaa banwo nu oo, anaa nwomaa, anaa ataadeɛ biala bɔ bafa nwomaa bapa nu oo, 49sɛ ngekalewa ne nye te nyaa monɛ anaa kɔkorɛ wɔ ataadeɛ ne anu a, kyɛ kundu anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ, anaa nwomaa, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa nwomaa bapa hɔ oo, ye de kwata anwonyerɛ ɔ, na odi kyɛ bɛfa bekyire ɔsɔfo ne. 50Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne neanea ngekalewa ne, na odi kyɛ ɔmaa bɛfa ataadeɛ ne ngome begua nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo; 51Ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea ngekalewa ne. Sɛ ngekalewa ne atrɛ wɔ ataadeɛ ne anu a, kyɛ kundu anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ, anaa nwomaa ne anu a, ye de né ɔmva ye nwo nikyee bɔ bɛfa nwomaa ne bɛyɔ ɔ, ngekalewa ne te kwata anwonyerɛ bɔ ɔtrɛ ɔ; ataadeɛ ne nwo nde. 52Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne yera ataadeɛ ne, kyɛ anwonyerɛ ne wɔ kundu nu oo, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ nu oo, anaa nwera nu oo, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa nwomaa bapa ɔ nu oo, ofikyɛ ɔte kwata anwonyerɛ bɔ ɔtrɛ ɔ; odi kyɛ bɛfa see bɛyera ye ɔ.
53“Nakoso sɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea ngekalewa ne, ná sɛ ngekalewa ne wandrɛ wɔ ataadeɛ ne anu, kyɛ kundu anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa nwomaa bapa ɔ nu a, 54ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔhyɛ maa bɛpo nikyee bɔ ngekalewa wɔ nu ne, ná afei ɔ́fa nikyee ne angome ógua nekaa bie ɛlɛsoo bieku. 55Sɛ bɛpo nikyee bɔ ngekalewa wɔ nu ne beyie a, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne nea nikyee ne. Na nekaa bɔ ngekalewa ne wɔ ne, sɛ berɛ anwosue ne tɛ te kyɛ bɔ ɔte hɔ a, ye de sɛ anwonyerɛ ne wandrɛ po a, ye nwo nde. Nekaa bɔ kwata ne ayɔ ne, kyɛ ɔwɔ ye nyunu oo, anaa ye si oo, odi kyɛ ɛfa see yera ataadeɛ ne.
56Nakoso sɛ bɛpo ataadeɛ ne beyie, ná ɔsɔfo ne nea ataadeɛ ne, ná anwonyerɛ ne abrɛ ase a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔte berɛ ne fi ataadeɛ ne anu, kyɛ kundu ahɔ oo anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ ahɔ oo, anaa nwomaa ahɔ oo. 57Nakoso sɛ ngekalewa ne sa ba ataadeɛ ne anu de a, kyɛ kundu anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa nwomaa bapa ɔ, ye de né anwonyerɛ ne ɔtrɛ; odi kyɛ ɛfa see yera nikyee bɔ ngekalewa ne wɔ nu ne. 58Nakoso sɛ bɛpo ataadeɛ ne, kyɛ kundu anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa gyese banwo ɔ, anaa nikyee biala bɔ bafa nwomaa bapa ɔ, ná sɛ ngekalewa ne fi nu tu a, odi kyɛ bɛpo ye bieku, na ataadeɛ ne nwo kɔte.”
59Mmeraa bɔ ɔfa kwata anwonyerɛ bɔ ɔwɔ ataadeɛ nu nwo ɛhe: kyɛ bafa boaen nwiaa anaa gyese banwo ɔ, anaa bɔ bafa kundu anaa nwomaa bapa ɔ. Ɛhe kɔmaa ekonwu kyɛ ye nwo te anaa ye nwo nde.

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
Kwatafoɛ nwo telɛ
1AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, 2 “Kyẽa bɔ bɛte kwataniɛ nwo ne, mmeraa bɔ ɔla berɛ ma ye ɛhe: Odi kyɛ bɛfa ye bɛbrɛ ɔsɔfo ne; 3na odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fi asikyeleɛ ne anu ofite kɔneanea sɔ sona ne anwo. Na sɛ kwataniɛ ne nwo asa afi kwata anwonyerɛ ne anwo a, 4ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne hyɛ maa ɔnate sona bɔ bɛbaate ye nwo ne ati bɛ́fa ɛhemɔ bɛ́ba: nnomaa nyɔ bɔ bɛte ngoa nu bɔ bɛ nwo te ɔ, bakaa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye sida, adaabene ne sufiɛ. 5Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne hyɛ maa bɛfa nnomaa nemɔ nu ko besinze kukue bɔ mbombonzue gua nu ɔ so ná beku ye. 6Anomaa ko bɔ ɔtɛte ngoa nu ne, odi kyɛ ɔfa ye boka bakaa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye sida ne, adaabene ne, ɔne sufiɛ ne aso. Na anomaa bɔ bɛfale ye besinzele mbombonzue nu nzue so behuni ye ne, ye mogya ne, odi kyɛ ɔfa bɛ ne anomaa bɔ ɔte ngoa nu ne owura nu. 7Na sona bɔ bɛ́te ye nwo béfi kwata anwonyerɛ nwo ne, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔfa mogya ne pete ye nwo pɛen nzoo. Afei odi kyɛ ɔfa to dwaa kyɛ sona ne nwo ate, ná ɔyakyi anomaa bɔ ɔte ngoa nu ne maa ɔkɔ buro. 8Sona bɔ bate ye nwo ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nningyein, ɔpoa ye nwo nwiaa amu, ɔfa nzue bia, na ye nwo kɔte. Ye si ye, odi kyɛ osa ba asikyeleɛ nu berɛ, nakoso ɔkɔtena ye ɛtena sua asi ɛlɛsoo. 9Na ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔpoa ye nwo nwiaa amukoraa: ye ti nwiaa, ye kanza ne ye ndo nwiaa; ɔ́poa ye nwo nwiaa amukoraa. Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ye nwo kɔte.
10Ye ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔfa mmoaen nyii akrɔngrɔma nyɔ bɔ bellili nnɛen biala, boaen beleɛ akrɔngrɔma ko bɔ wali afoɛ ko bɔ ollili nnɛen biala ɔ, esam paa olonka nza bɔ bafa ngoo bafra bɔ bɛ́fa bɛ́bɔ aburoo afɔleɛ ɔ, ɔne ngoo towaa ko. 11Na ɔsɔfo bɔ ɔte sɔ sona ne anwo ne, ɔkɔfa sɔ sona ne ɔne sɔ nningyein nemɔ kɔhɔ AWURADE nyunu wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anoa nu berɛ. 12Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa mmoaen akrɔngrɔma nyii nemɔ anu ko ɔboka ngoo towaa ko so, ná ɔfa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ. Odi kyɛ ɔpagya so fa bɔ ɛnwahanɛ afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 13Odi kyɛ oku boaen akrɔngrɔma ne wɔ nekaa krongron berɛ, nekaa bɔ beku bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ɔne naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ngaka ne, ofikyɛ foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ te kyɛ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ne ala; ɔte ɔsɔfo ne deɛ na ɔte krongron paa. 14Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔfa foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ mogya ne bie, ná ɔfa kekã sona bɔ bɛbaate ye nwo ne ye so famaa tɛndiaa ne, ye sa kokotire famaa ɔne ye gya kokotire famaa. 15Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa ngoo towaa ne, ná ohwie ngoo ne bie gua ye bɔbɔ ye sa bɛen nu, 16ná ɔ́fa ye sa mmɛseka famaa ne bɔ ngoo bɔ ɔwɔ ye sa bɛen nu ne anu, ná ɔfa ye sa mmɛseka pete ngoo ne bie pɛen nzoo, AWURADE nyunu. 17Ngoo bɔ ɔkɔha ɔsɔfo ne sa nu ne, odi kyɛ ɔfa bie kekã sona bɔ bɛbaate ye nwo ne ye so famaa tɛndiaa ne, ye sa kokotire famaa, ɔne ye gya kokotire famaa, wɔ foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ mogya ne aso. 18Ngoo bɔ ɔkɔha ɔsɔfo ne sa nu ne, odi kyɛ ohwie gua sona bɔ bɛwɔ so bɛte ye nwo ne ye ti so. Afei ɔsɔfo ne ɔ́yɛ mbata ɔ́ma ye wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 19Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ fa yɛ mbata ma sona bɔ ye nwo agua fiɛ ne, ná ye nwo te. Na ɛhe asi ne, odi kyɛ oku naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ kaka ne, 20ná ɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ, ɔne aburoo afɔleɛ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso. Ɔnate ɛhe aso, ɔsɔfo ne ɔ́pata ma ye ma ye nwo te.
21“Nakoso sɛ sona ne te ehianiɛ ná ye nwo ngɔso so a, ye de odi kyɛ ɔfa boaen nyii akrɔngrɔma ko bayɛ foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ bɔ bɛkɔnwanha ye bɛkɔyɛ mbata bɛkɔma ye ɔ. Nningyein hemɔ koso boka so: esam paa bɔ bafa ngoo bafra ɔ olonka ko bɔ bɛfa bɛbɔ aburoo afɔleɛ ɔ, ngoo towaa ko; 22mmorɔma nyɔ anaa mmorɔnoma buruwa nyɔ bɔ ye nwo kɔsõ so ɔ: ko te bɔne nwo afɔleɛ yeɛ ko ne koso te naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ. 23Ye ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔfa bɛ brɛ ɔsɔfo ne ma ɔfa te ye nwo wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anoa nu berɛ, AWURADE nyunu. 24Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔfa foɛlilɛ boaen akrɔngrɔma ne, ɔne ngoo towaa ko, ná ɔpagya bɛ fa bɔ ɛnwahanɛ afɔleɛ wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 25Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne oku foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ boaen ne, ná ɔfa foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ mogya ne bie fa kekã sona bɔ bɛwɔ so bɛte ye nwo ne ye so famaa tɛndiaa ne, ye sa kokotire famaa ne ɔne ye gya kokotire famaa. 26Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne hwie ngoo ne bie gua ye bɔbɔ ye sa bɛen nu; 27ná ɔ́fa ye sa mmɛseka famaa pete ngoo bɔ ɔwɔ ye sa bɛen anu ne bie ne pɛen nzoo, AWURADE nyunu. 28Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne ɔfa ngoo bɔ ɔwɔ ye sa nu ne bie kekã sona bɔ bɛwɔ so bɛte ye nwo ne ye so famaa tɛndiaa ne, ye sa kokotire famaa, ɔne ye gya kokotire famaa wɔ nekaa bɔ ɔfale foɛlilɛ afɔleɛ mogya ɔkekane ne. 29Ngoo bɔ ɔkɔha ɔsɔfo ne sa nu ne, odi kyɛ ohwie gua sona bɔ bɛwɔ so bɛte ye nwo ne ti so, ná ɔfa pata ma ye wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 30Mmorɔma anaa mmorɔnoma buruwa bɔ sona ne nwo kɔsõ so ne, ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa bɔ afɔleɛ. 31Nnomaa ne bɔ sona ne nwo kɔsõ so ne, ko te bɔne nwo afɔleɛ yeɛ ko koso te naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ; sona bɔ bɛwɔ so bɛte ye nwo ne, odi kyɛ ɔfa aburoo afɔleɛ boka so, ná ɔsɔfo ne ɔpata ma ye wɔ AWURADE nyunu. 32Sona bɔ kwata anwonyerɛ kɔyɛ ye nakoso ye nwo ngɔso nningyein bɔ bɛfa bɛbɔ afɔleɛ bɛpete ye nwo ne, sɔ mmeraa he yeɛ ɔla berɛ ma ye ɔ.”
33AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, 34“Sɛ ɛmɔbadwu Kanaan aseɛ bɔ méfa méma ɛmɔ maa ɔyɛ ɛmɔ deɛ ne aso, ná sɛ mema kwata anwonyerɛ pe awuro bie anu wɔ aseɛ bɔ ɛmɔ sa baahã ye ne aso a, 35odi kyɛ awuro ne mene kɔka kyire ɔsɔfo ne kyɛ, ‘Ɔyɛ me kyɛ anwonyerɛ bie ape m’awuro dɔ.’ 36Na ɔsɔfo ne kɔhyɛ maa bɛkɔyeye awuro ne anu nningyein amukoraa koraka ne ɔsɔfo ne ahɔ wanea anwonyerɛ ne. Sɛ banyɔ sɔ a, awuro berɛ nningyein amukoraa nwo kogua fiɛ. Ye si ye, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne kɔneanea awuro ne anu. 37Odi kyɛ ɔkɔnea; sɛ anwonyerɛ ne wakekã awuro ne terɛ ne anwo ma berɛ ayɛ kyɛ apopobibire anaa kɔkorɛ, ná sɛ osoma kyɛ wadidi wahɔ terɛ ne anu a, 38ye de odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo fa anoa nu berɛ fite, ná ɔto awuro ne anu ɛlɛsoo. 39Ye ɛlɛsoo ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo sa kɔneanea berɛ; sɛ anwonyerɛ ne atrɛ wɔ awuro ne ye trɛ ne anwo a, 40odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne hyɛ kyɛ, nyɔboɛ mɔ bɔ anwonyerɛ ne ayɛ bɛ nwo ne, bɛ́yeye béfi sua ne anu ná beegyi bégua kuro ne asi dɔ nekaa bie bɔ berɛ nde ɔ. 41Odi kyɛ ɔmaa bɛwɔngye awuro ne akunu amukoraa. Ye kunu bɔ bɛkɔwɔngye ne, ɔsɛ kyɛ bekogyi begua kuro ne asi dɔ nekaa bie bɔ berɛ ɔnde ɔ. 42Odi kyɛ bɛsesa nyɔboɛ foforɛ bewura nyɔboɛ ɛhene mɔ boso, ná bɛ́fa ɛfaa foforɛ bɛma awuro ne anwo.
43“Sɛ bɛyeye nyɔboɛ ne, ná bɛwɔngyewɔngye terɛ ne anwo, ná bɛma awuro ne anwo beyie, ná ye si ye anwonyerɛ ne sa ba awuro berɛ a, 44odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne kɔnea awuro berɛ. Na sɛ anwonyerɛ ne atrɛ wɔ awuro berɛ a, ye de né kwata anwonyerɛ bɔ ɔtrɛ yeɛ wape awuro berɛ ɔ, awuro ne nwo nde. 45Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne maa bedwiri awuro ne begua ase; ná ɔmaa bɛsesa nu nyɔboɛ, mmakaa ne nnɛterɛ amukoraa bekogyi begua kuro ne asi dɔ nekaa bɔ berɛ ɔnde ɔ. 46Mmerɛ bɔ bato awuro ne anu ne, ebiala bɔ ɔkɔhɔ nu ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 47Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔla sɔ awuro ne anu ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, na ebiala bɔ okodidi awuro berɛ ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein.
48“Nakoso sɛ bɛma awuro ne anwo beyie, ná ye si ye ɔsɔfo ne banea ná anwonyerɛ ne wandrɛ wɔ awuro berɛ a, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa to dwaa kyɛ awuro ne ye nwo te; anwonyerɛ ne ahɔ. 49Sɛ bɛte awuro ne anwo a, odi kyɛ ɔfa nnomaa nyɔ boka bakaa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye sida ne, adaabene ne sufiɛ so. 50Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔfa nnomaa nemɔ nu ko osinze kukue bɔ mbombonzue gua nu ɔ so, ná oku ye. 51Odi kyɛ ɔfa bakaa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye sida ne, sufiɛ ne, adaabene ne ɔne anomaa bɔ ɔtɛte ngoa nu ne, ná ɔ́fa bɛ wura anomaa bɔ bahu ye ne mogya ne anu, ɔne mbombonzue ne anu, ná ɔfa ɔpete awuro berɛ pɛen nzoo. 52Atee he aso yeɛ ɔsɔfo ne kɔfa anomaa mogya ne, mbombonzue ne, anomaa bɔ ɔtɛte ase ne, bakaa bɔ bɛfrɛ ye sida ne, sufiɛ ne ɔne adaabene ne kɔte awuro ne anwo ɔ. 53Odi kyɛ ɔyakyi anomaa bɔ ɔtɛte ngoa nu ne wɔ kuro ne tiwaa maa ɔkɔ buro. Ɔnate ɛhe aso, ɔkɔpata kɔma awuro ne, na awuro ne anwo kɔte.
54Mmeraa bɔ ɔla berɛ ma kwata anwonyerɛ biala ɛhe: asee, 55kwata bɔ ɔwɔ ataadeɛ nu, anaa awuro nu, 56edoee anaa yira anaa ndotɔndotɔ. 57Ɛhemɔ yeɛ ɔkɔmaa bekonwu kyɛ nikyee bie nwo te anaakyɛ ye nwo nde ɔ. Kwata anwonyerɛ mɔ nwo mmeraa ɛhe.

Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.

And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
translation_text:
Bɛ nwo nzue senɛ nwo dwirɛ
1Na AWURADE sele Mose ne Aarɔn kyɛ, 2“Ɛ́mɔhã behyire Yisrael ama kyɛ, ‘Sɛ ebie bienzua fiti a, sɔ nzue ne ma ye nwo gua fiɛ. 3Nzue bɔ opukye ma ye nwo gua fiɛ ne, ye nwo mmeraa ɛhe: sɛ ye nwo nzue ne ɔtɛsẽ oo, anaakyɛ ye bienzua nu atee tua oo, ɔte nikyee bɔ ɔma ye nwo gua fiɛ ɔ. 4Na bɛen biala bɔ sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti ne kɔla so ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ; yeɛ nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔtena so ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ. 5Na ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha ye bɛen ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo ɔnde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 6Nikyee biala bɔ sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti watena so ne, sona biala bɔ ɔkɔtena so ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue obia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 7Na ebiala bɔ ɔkɔfa ye nwo kɔha sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 8Sɛ sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti ne, ɔfe nwɔserɛ gua sona bɔ ye nwo te nwo a, odi kyɛ sɔ sona ne po ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 9Sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti ne, afupɔngɔ so atɛ biala bɔ ɔkɔtena so ne, ɔkɔyɛ nikyee bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ. 10Ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha nikyee biala bɔ watena so ne, ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa; na ebiala bɔ ɔkɔsoa sɔ nikyee ne odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 11Ebiala bɔ ye bienzua fiti ne, sɛ wamva nzue wanwunzi ye sa koraka, ná ɔfa ye nwo ka ebie a, odi kyɛ sɔ sona ne po ye nwo nningyein ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 12Kukue biala, sɛ sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti nwo ka ye a, odi kyɛ bɛbɔ ye; yeɛ sɛ ye nwo ka alaka biala bɔ bafa bakaa bayɔ a, odi kyɛ bɛfa nzue benwunzi ye nwo.
13“Sona bɔ ye bienzua fiti ne, sɛ ye nwo sa a, odi kyɛ otu ɛlɛsoo sie berɛ fa pete ye nwo. Afei odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein ná ɔ́fa mbombonzue gyengɔɔ obia, na ye nwo kɔte. 14Ye ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne aso, odi kyɛ ɔfa mmorɔma nyɔ anaa mmorɔnoma buruwa nyɔ ɔba AWURADE nyunu wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ, ná ɔ́fa bɛ ma ɔsɔfo ne. 15Na afei odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa nnomaa nemɔ ko bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ná ɔ́fa ko koso ɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ. Ɔsɔfo ne kogyina sona ne gya nu kɔpata kɔma ye wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu, ɔnate ye bienzua bɔ né ofiti ne ati.
16“Sɛ bienzua bie nwo nzue ba a, odi kyɛ ɔfa nzue bia ye nwo amukoraati, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 17Nikyee biala bɔ bafa ɛtena anaa nwomaa bapa ne, sɛ ye nwo nzue ne bie gua so a, ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛfa nzue bɛpo, na ɔkɔyɛ nikyee bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 18Sɛ bienzua bie ne brasua bɛda, ná ye nwo nzue ba a, ɔsɛ kyɛ bɛ munyɔ bɛfa nzue bebia, na bɛ nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa.
19“Sɛ brasua bu ye sa a, ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ ɛlɛsoo, na ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha sɔ sona nen, ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 20Nikyee biala bɔ sɔ brasua ne kɔla so wɔ mmerɛ bɔ wabu ye sa ne, ɔkɔyɛ nikyee bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ; yeɛ nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔtena so ne koso, ɔkɔyɛ nikyee bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ. 21Sɔ brasua ne, ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha ye bɛen ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 22Ebiala bɔ ye nwo kɔha nikyee biala bɔ sɔ brasua ne kɔtena so ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 23Sɛ bɛen oo, anaa nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔtena so oo, sɛ ebie nwo ka ye a, ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 24 Sɛ bienzua bie ne ye bɛda, na nikyee bɔ wama ye nwo agua fiɛ ne bie ka bienzua ne a, bienzua ne nwo kogua fiɛ ɛlɛsoo, na bɛen biala bɔ sɔ bienzua ne kɔla so ne nwo kogua fiɛ.
25“Sɛ brasua nwu mogya nyunu ngyẽa pee wɔ aberɛ bɔ nna ye sabulɛ mmerɛ ahɔ ɔ a, anaa obu ye sa maa ɔtra kyẽa bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ ofi ne a, mmerɛ bɔ onwu mogya nyunu ne amukoraati, ɔkɔhɔ so kɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ, kyɛ mmerɛ bɔ ɔfa bu ye sa ne ala, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ. 26Mmerɛ bɔ ɔtɛnwu mogya nyunu ne amukoraati, bɛen biala bɔ ɔkɔla so ne, bekobu bɛen ne kyɛ ye nwo nde, kyɛ ye bɛen bɔ ɔkɔla so mmerɛ bɔ wabu ye sa ne ala; na nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔtena so ne, ye nwo kogua fiɛ, kyɛ mmerɛ bɔ wabu ye sa ne ala. 27Ebiala bɔ ɔkɔfa ye nwo kɔha sɔ nningyein nemɔ nen, ye nwo kogua fiɛ; odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔfa nzue bia, na ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ maa okoodwu nɔsoa. 28Nakoso sɛ mogya bɔ wanwu ye nyunu ne pɛ a, odi kyɛ ɔma ɛlɛsoo pɛ nu, na ye si ye ɔkɔyɛ sona bɔ ye nwo te ɔ. 29Ye ɛlɛbɔtwɛ ne aso, odi kyɛ braa ne fa mmubure nyɔ anaa mmorɔnoma buruwa nyɔ brɛ ɔsɔfo ne wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ. 30Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne fa ko bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ, ná ɔfa ko koso bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ; na ɔsɔfo ne kɔpata kɔma ye wɔ AWURADE nyunu, ɔnate mogya bɔ onwuni ye nyunu maa ye nwo guale fiɛ ne ati.
31“Sɔa yeɛ odi kyɛ ɛmɔyɔ bɛfa bɛte Yisraelfoɛ nwo befi nningyein bɔ ogua bɛ nwo fiɛ nwo ɔ, amaa bamva efiɛ banga me ɛtena sua ne, ná ɔnate bɛ nwo bɔ wagua fiɛ ne ati banwuwu.”
32Mmeraa he yeɛ ɔla berɛ ma bienzua biala bɔ ye bienzua kofiti, anaa bienzua biala bɔ ye nwo nzue kɔwa maa ye nwo kogua fiɛ ɔ, 33ɔne brasua biala bɔ okobu ye sa, bienzua anaa brasua biala bɔ ye nwo nzue kogua, yeɛ bienzua biala bɔ ɔne brasua bɔ ye nwo nde kɔla ɔ.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Mbata kyẽa
1Aarɔn mma mmienzua nyɔ hɔle AWURADE nyunu ná bewuli ne, ye si ye, AWURADE ne Mose dwudwole. 2 Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, “Ka kyire eliɛma Aarɔn kyɛ, nekaa krongron bɔ ɔwɔ mbɛmuɛ tena ne asi dɔ ne, mbata bia bɔ ɔwɔ apam alaka ne aso ne, nnɛmaa ɔba ye nyunu mmerɛ biala bɔ okuro ɔ. Sɛ ɔyɔ sɔ a okowu, ofikyɛ meye me nwo ali mekyire wɔ munungum bɔ ɔwɔ mbata bia ne aso ne anu. 3Sɛ Aarɔn ɔba nekaa krongron ne anu a, bɔ odi kyɛ ɔyɔ ɛhe: odi kyɛ ɔfa nandwie nyii akrɔngrɔma ko bɔ ɔfa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ɔ ɔne boaen nyii bɔ ɔfa bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ. 4Odi kyɛ owura nwera ataadeɛ tendenn krongron ne, ná owura nwera pieto ɔfa kata ye nwo, ná ɔbɔ nwera abɔsoɛ ne, ná ɔbɔ nwera abotire ne; ɛhemɔ te ndaadeɛ krongron. Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔfa nzue bia koraka né wawura ndaadeɛ nemɔ. 5Odi kyɛ ode mbɔngye nyii nyɔ fi Yisrael maen berɛ bɔ ɔfa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ɔ, ɔne boaen nyii ko bɔ ɔfa bɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ɔ.
6“Odi kyɛ Aarɔn fa nandwie nyii ne bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ma ye nwo, ná ɔpata ma ye bɔbɔ ye nwo, ɔne ye awuro ama. 7Ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔfa mbɔngye nyii nyɔ nemɔ ba AWURADE nyunu wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ. 8Odi kyɛ Aarɔn to mbɔngye nyɔ nemɔ aso serewa; ko te AWURADE deɛ, yeɛ ko koso te Asasɛl deɛ. 9Odi kyɛ Aarɔn fa abɔngye bɔ serewa ne yele ye mane AWURADE ne, ná ɔfa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ; 10nakoso abɔngye ko bɔ serewa ne yele ye mane Asasɛl ne de, odi kyɛ bɛfa ye bɔ ɔte ngoa nu ɔ bɛba AWURADE nyunu bɛbayɛ mbata, ná bɛkɔɔyakyi ye ɛserɛ so bɛma Asasɛl.
11“Odi kyɛ Aarɔn fa nandwie nyii ne ɔbɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ma ye nwo, ná ɔpata ma ye nwo ne ye awuro ama. Ɔsɛ kyɛ oku nandwie nyii ne ná ɔfa bɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ma ye nwo. 12Na odi kyɛ ɔfa see kulie bɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne anu see gonn ayi ye tɛkyɛ ɔ ɔba AWURADE nyunu, ɔne ɛyɛɛ fona muhumuhu bɛ sa bum nyɔ, ná ɔ́fa bra mbɛmuɛ tena ne asi. 13Afei odi kyɛ ɔfa ɛyɛɛ ne ogua see ne aso wɔ AWURADE nyunu, amaa mbata bia bɔ ɔwɔ Adanzeɛ ne aso ne, ɛyɛɛ nwosina ne akata so, ná wanwu. 14Odi kyɛ ɔfa nandwie nyii mogya ne bie, ná ɔfa ye sa mmɛseka bɔ nu fa pete mbata bia ne anyunu; ɔ́fa ye sa mmɛseka ne pete mogya ne pɛen nzoo.
15“Odi kyɛ oku maen bɔne nwo afɔleɛ abɔngye ne, ná ɔ́fa ye mogya ne ɔba mbɛmuɛ ɛtena ne asi. Kyɛbɔ ɔfale nandwie nyii mogya ne yɔle ne, sɔ ala yeɛ odi kyɛ ɔfa abɔngye mogya ne ɔyɔ ɔ; ɔsɛ kyɛ ɔfa mogya ne pete mbata bia ne aso ne ye nyunu. 16Sɔa yeɛ odi kyɛ ɔyɔ mbata ma nekaa krongron ne ɔ, ɔnate Yisrael ama bɛ nwo bɔ wagua fiɛ, bɛ mmeraatolɛ, ɔne bɛ bɔne amukoraa ti. Sɔ ala yeɛ odi kyɛ ɔyɔ ma ɛtena sua atenaleɛ bɔ ɔwɔ mmenia bɔ bɛ nwo nde ne b’afia ne ɔ. 17Ofi mmerɛ bɔ ɔsɔfo ne kowura ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anu kyɛ ɔkwaayɛ mbata wɔ nekaa krongron ne anu ne, kɔpem kyɛ ɔkɔpata kɔma ye bɔbɔ ye nwo, ye awuro ama ɔne Yisrael maen ne amukoraati, ná okofite ne, onni kyɛ ebiala kɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anu. 18Na odi kyɛ ofite ɔkɔ afɔleɛ bokyea bɔ ɔwɔ AWURADE nyunu ne anwo, ná ɔpata ma afɔleɛ bokyea ne; odi kyɛ ɔfa nandwie nyii mogya ne bie, ɔne abɔngye mogya ne bie kekã afɔleɛ bokyea mmɛen ne anu biala nwo bra yia. 19Odi kyɛ ɔfa ye sa mmɛseka pete mogya ne bie gua so pɛen nzoo, ná ɔte ye nwo ɔyɛ ye krongron fi Yisraelfoɛ nwo bɔ wagua fiɛ ne anwo.
20“Sɛ ɔsɔfo ne yɛ mbata ma nekaa krongron ne, ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne, ɔne afɔleɛ bokyea ne yie a, odi kyɛ ɔfa abɔngye bɔ ɔte ngoa nu ne ɔba. 21Afei odi kyɛ Aarɔn fa ye sa munyɔ gua abɔngye bɔ ɔte ngoa nu ne ye ti afia, ná ɔka Yisraelfoɛ amumuyɛɛ amukoraa, bɛ mmeraatolɛ amukoraa ɔne bɛ bɔne amukoraa gua abɔngye ne aso, ná ɔprapra ye mukoraati gua ye so. Odi kyɛ ɔyakyi abɔngye ne ma bienzua bie bɔ bafa sɔ adwuma ne bawura ye sa maa berɛ ne ala ɔkɔyakyi kaka ne eburo maa ɔkɔ. 22Yisraelfoɛ bɛ bɔne amukoraa, abɔngye ne kɔsoa kɔhɔ aseɛ bɔ kuro sona biala ɔtte so ɔ so; na odi kyɛ ɔkɔyakyi abɔngye ne wɔ eburo dɔ.
23“Odi kyɛ Aarɔn wura ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne anu, ná opuro nwera ataadeɛ bɔ owurale koraka yeɛ ɔkɔ nekaa krongron ne, ná ɔyakyi bɛ berɛ. 24Na odi kyɛ ɔfa nzue obia wɔ nekaa bɔ ɔte krongron ɔ, ná owura ye ataadeɛ ne, ná osa ofite babɔ ye naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ, ɔne maen naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ ne, ná ɔpata ma ye bɔbɔ ye nwo ɔne maen ne. 25Ɛloe bɔ ɔwɔ bɔne nwo afɔleɛ ne anu ne, odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne yera ye wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso. 26Sona bɔ ɔyɛ a, ɔkɔyakyi abɔngye ne ma Asasɛl ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye ndaadeɛ ná ɔfa nzue bia koraka né wahora wawa asikyeleɛ ne anu. 27 Bɔne nwo afɔleɛ nandwie nyii ne, ɔne bɔne nwo afɔleɛ abɔngye ne bɔ bɛfale bɛ mogya bɛɛpatale wɔ nekaa krongron ne anu ne, odi kyɛ bɛfa bɛ bɛkɔ asikyeleɛ ne asi; na bɛ nwomaa, bɛ naen ɔne bɛ fure ne, odi kyɛ bɛfa see bɛyera bɛ. 28Sona bɔ ɔkɔyera bɛ ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye ndaadeɛ ná ɔ́fa nzue bia koraka né wahora wawa asikyeleɛ ne anu.
29 “Odi kyɛ ɛhe yɛ ahyɛdeɛ ma ɛmɔ: bosome nzoo ne, ye kyẽa bɔ ɔtɔ so buru ne, odi kyɛ ɛmɔkye ɛhɔen; kuromani oo, ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ waatena ɛmɔ nu oo, nnɛma ebiala yɔ adwuma biala. 30Ofikyɛ sɔ kyẽa ne yeɛ bɛpata bɛma ɛmɔ, ná bɛfa bɛte ɛmɔ nwo befi ɛmɔ bɔne amukoraa nwo, ma ɛmɔ nwo te wɔ AWURADE nyunu ɔ. 31Ɔte afofikyẽa bɔ odi mu paa ma ɛmɔ ɔ. Odi kyɛ ɛmɔkye ɛhɔen; ɔte ahyɛdeɛ afebɔɔ. 32Ɔsɔfo bɔ bapopa ye ngoo ná bate ye nwo maa waasi ye baba gya nu wayɛ ɔsɔfo ne, ye yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ mbata ne ɔ; odi kyɛ owura nwera ataadeɛ krongron ne. 33Odi kyɛ ɔpata ma nekaa krongron ne, ɛtena sua atenaleɛ ne, ɔne afɔleɛ bokyea ne; ná afei ɔ́pata ɔ́ma asɔfo nemɔ, ɔne maen ne amukoraa. 34Ɛhe te ahyɛdeɛ afebɔɔ ma ɛmɔ: afoɛ biala odi kyɛ ɛmɔyɛ Yisraelfoɛ bɛ bɔne amukoraa nwo mbata ko. Na Mose yɔle kyɛbɔ AWURADE hyɛle ye ne.

english_text:
Where To Offer Sacrifices
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell Aaron, his sons, and everyone else in Israel:
3-4Whenever you kill any of your cattle, sheep, or goats as sacrifices to me, you must do it at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you don't, you will be guilty of pouring out blood, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 5And so, when you sacrifice an animal to ask my blessing, it must not be done out in a field, 6but in front of the sacred tent. Then a priest can splatter its blood against the bronze altar and send its fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 7Don't ever turn from me again and offer sacrifices to goat-demons. This law will never change.
8Remember! No one in Israel, including foreigners, is to offer a sacrifice anywhere 9except at the entrance to the sacred tent. If you do, you will no longer belong to my people.
Do Not Eat Blood
The Lord said:
10 I will turn against any of my people who eat blood. This also includes any foreigners living among you. 11 Life is in the blood, and I have given you the blood of animals to sacrifice in place of your own. 12That's also why I have forbidden you to eat blood. 13Even if you should hunt and kill a bird or an animal, you must drain out the blood and cover it with soil.
14The life of every living creature is in its blood. That's why I have forbidden you to eat blood and why I have warned you that anyone who does will no longer belong to my people.
15If you happen to find a dead animal and eat it, you must take a bath and wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening. 16If you don't take a bath, you will suffer for what you did wrong.
translation_text:
Afɔleɛ nwo mmeraa biemɔ
1Na AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, 2“Ka kyire Aarɔn ne ye mma mmienzua, ɔne Yisraelfoɛ amukoraa kyɛ, ‘Bɔ AWURADE ahyɛ hɔ ɛhe: 3Yisrael awuro ama ne, sɛ ebie ku nandwie anaa boaen akrɔngrɔma anaa abɔngye wɔ asikyeleɛ nu berɛ, anaa wɔ asikyeleɛ ne asi, 4ná wamva ye wamma ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ, wamma ammɔ afɔleɛ wamma AWURADE wɔ AWURADE ɛtena sua ne anyunu a, okoli mogya hagualɛ nwo fɔ. Waha mogya wagua, na odi kyɛ bɛpɛ ye asue befi maen ne anu. 5Ɛhe kɔma Yisraelfoɛ kɔfa b’afɔleɛ bɔ bɛbɔ ye wɔ ɛserɛ so ne bɛkɔbrɛ AWURADE. Odi kyɛ bɛfa bɛbrɛ ɔsɔfo ne maa ɔfa ma AWURADE wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ, ná ɔ́fa bɔ asomdwee afɔleɛ ma AWURADE. 6Odi kyɛ ɔsɔfo ne hwie mogya ne gua AWURADE afɔleɛ bokyea ne anwo wɔ ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ, ná ɔ́yera ɛloe ne maa ɔyɛ nwosina bɔ ɔbo AWURADE fona ɔ. 7Ɔnate ɛhe aso bɛngɔhɔ so bɛngɔbɔ b’afɔleɛ mɔ bɛngɔma mmosoen mɔ bɔ besoma mbɔngye ne, mekyire mmosoen bɔ bafa bɛ nwo bawura bɛ sa ne. Ɛhe kɔyɛ ahyɛdeɛ afebɔɔ kɔma bɛ wɔ b’aworɛ ndoatoasoɛ mukoraati nu.’
8“Na sá ka kyire bɛ kyɛ, ‘Ebiala bɔ ofi Yisrael awuro anaakyɛ ɛwɔfoɛ biala bɔ waatena Yisraelfoɛ nu, sɛ ɔbɔ naen yeralɛ afɔleɛ, anaa ɔbɔ afɔleɛ biala, 9ná wamva wamma ɛtena sua atenaleɛ anoa nu berɛ wamma ammɔ afɔleɛ ne wamma AWURADE a, odi kyɛ bɛpɛ ye asue befi maen ne anu.
Onni kyɛ bedi mogya
10 “Sɛ ebiala bɔ ofi Yisrael awuro anaakyɛ ɛwɔfoɛ mɔ bɔ baatena bɛ nu, odi mogya biala a, ngotu me nye ngosie sɔ sona ne aso, na ngɔpɛ ye asue ngofi maen ne anu. 11 Ofikyɛ anwoɔnaen biala, ye ngoa wɔ ye mogya nu; na mafa mogya mama ɛmɔ wɔ afɔleɛ bokyea ne aso kyɛ ɛ́mɔfa bɛ́yɛ mbata bɛ́ma ɛmɔ kra. Ngoa wɔ mogya nu, yiti mogya yeɛ odi kyɛ bɛfa bɛyɛ mbata ɔ. 12Yiti mahã mahyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, ‘Nnɛma ɛmɔ nu biala di mogya, yeɛ nnɛma ɛwɔfoɛ biala bɔ waatena ɛmɔ nu koso di mogya. 13Na Yisraelniɛ biala anaa ɛwɔfoɛ biala bɔ waatena ɛmɔ nu ne, sɛ oku kaka anaa anomaa biala bɔ bedi a, odi kyɛ ohwie ye mogya gua ase ná otu nnɛterɛ kata so.
14“Ofikyɛ anwoɔnaen biala, ye mogya yeɛ ɔte ye ngoa ɔ; yiti mahã mahyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, Nnɛma ɛmɔdi abɔdeɛ biala ye mogya, ofikyɛ anwoɔnaen biala ye mogya yeɛ ɔte ye ngoa ɔ; na ebiala bɔ okoli mogya ne, odi kyɛ bɛpɛ ye asue. 15Sona biala, kuromani oo, ɛwɔfoɛ oo, bɔ okoli naenmvuin anaa naen biala bɔ kaka aboyaa bie ahu ye atete ye ne, odi kyɛ ɔpo ye nwo nningyein, ná ɔ́fa nzue bia, na ye nwo kogua fiɛ maa okoodwu nɔsoa koraka né ye nwo ate. 16Nakoso sɛ wambo ye ndaadeɛ anaakyɛ wammia a, ye de, ye musue kɔbɔ ye ti so.

english_text:
Forbidden Sex
1The Lord told Moses 2to tell the people of Israel:
I am the Lord your God! 3So don't follow the customs of Egypt where you used to live or those of Canaan where I am bringing you. 4I am the Lord your God, and you must obey my teachings. 5 Obey them and you will live. I am the Lord.
6Don't have sex with any of your close relatives, 7especially your own mother. This would disgrace your father. 8 And don't disgrace him by having sex with any of his other wives. 9 Don't have sex with your sister or stepsister, whether you grew up together or not. 10Don't disgrace yourself by having sex with your granddaughter 11or half sister 12-13 or a sister of your father or mother. 14Don't disgrace your uncle by having sex with his wife. 15 Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law 16 or sister-in-law. 17 And don't have sex with the daughter or granddaughter of any woman that you have earlier had sex with. You will be having sex with her closest relatives, and that would make you unclean. 18As long as your wife is alive, don't cause trouble for her by taking one of her sisters as a second wife.
19 When a woman is having her monthly period, she is unclean, so don't have sex with her.
20 Don't have sex with another man's wife—that would make you unclean.
21 Don't sacrifice your children on the altar fires to the god Molech. I am the Lord your God, and that would disgrace me.
22 It is disgusting for a man to have sex with another man.
23 Anyone who has sex with an animal is unclean.
24Don't make yourselves unclean by any of these disgusting practices of those nations that I am forcing out of the land for you. They made themselves 25and the land so unclean, that I punished the land because of their sins, and I made it vomit them up. 26-27Now don't do these sickening things that make the land filthy. Instead, obey my laws and teachings. 28Then the land won't become sick of you and vomit you up, just as it did them. 29-30If any of you do these vulgar, disgusting things, you will be unclean and no longer belong to my people. I am the Lord your God, and I forbid you to follow their sickening way of life.
translation_text:
Nnaa nu akyiwadeɛ
1AWURADE sele Mose kyɛ, 2“Ka kyire Yisraelfoɛ kyɛ, ‘Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ. 3Misraim aseɛ bɔ né ɛmɔte so ne, nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ bɛ yɔleɛ ne bie, yeɛ Kanaan aseɛ bɔ méfa ɛmɔ mékɔ so ne, bɛ yɔleɛ ne, nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ bie. Nnɛma ɛmɔdi b’ahyɛdeɛ so. 4Ɛ́mɔli me nhyehyɛleɛ ne m’ahyɛdeɛ so, ná ɛ́mɔfa bɛ́bɔ bɛ bra: Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ. 5 Yiti ɛ́mɔli m’ahyɛdeɛ ne me nhyehyɛleɛ so, na sona bɔ okoli so ne, okonya ngoa: Me ole AWURADE.
6“Nnɛma ɛmɔ nu biala ne ye abusuaniɛ beyia nnaa. Me ole AWURADE. 7 Nnɛne eni bɛda ná ɛfa gua ɛse nyunu ase; eni ɛne, nnɛne ye bɛda. 8 Nnɛne ɛse aye bɛda; ɛse aye ɛne. 9 Nnɛne eliɛma brasua, bɔ yeɛ ɔte ɛse awa brasua anaa eni awa brasua bɛda, kyɛ bɛwole ye awuro berɛ oo, anaa bɛwole ye nekaa bie oo. 10Nnɛne ɛwa bienzua awa brasua bɛda, ofikyɛ wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ mogya ɔ, na ɔte nyanzoen nikye. 11Nnɛne ɛse aye awa brasua, bɔ ɛse yeɛ ɔwole ye ɔ bɛda, ofikyɛ eliɛma brasua ɔ. 12 Nnɛne ɛse aliɛma brasua bɛda; ɛse ne ye bɛte mogya ko. 13Nnɛne eni aliɛma brasua bɛda, ofikyɛ eni ne ye bɛte mogya ko. 14 Nnɛne ɛse aliɛma bienzua aye bɛda, nnɛkɔ ɔye anwo; wɔ maame ɛne. 15 Nnɛne wɔ sia brasua bɛda; ɛwa bienzua aye ɛne; nnɛne ye bɛda. 16 Nnɛne eliɛma bienzua aye bɛda; eliɛma bienzua aye ɛne. 17 Nnɛne brasua bɛda ná esa ne ɔwa brasua koso bɛda; yeɛ nnɛne ye anomaa brasua bɛda; ɛne bɛ bayɛ mogya ko, yiti ɔte musue. 18Yeɛ nnɛgya brasua boka oliɛma brasua so, nnɛne ye da wɔ aberɛ bɔ oliɛma brasua ne tɛ te ase ɔ.
19 “Nnɛkɔ brasua nwo ɛne ye bɛda wɔ mmerɛ bɔ wabu ye sa ɔ. 20Nnɛne ebiɛngo aye bɛda, ná angua wɔ ne brasua ne nwo fiɛ. 21 Nnɛfa wɔ mma mɔ nu biala maa bɛfa see bɛyera ye bɛbɔ afɔleɛ bɛma bosoen Moleke, amaa ɔnate so angua wɔ Nyameɛ dumaa nwo fiɛ. Me ole AWURADE. 22 Nnɛma bienzua biala ɔne bienzua bɛda kyɛbɔ ɔne brasua bɛda ɔ; ɔte musue. 23 Nnɛma bienzua ɔne kaka bɛda ná ɔnate so wangua ye bɔbɔ ye nwo fiɛ; yeɛ nnɛma brasua biala fa ye nwo ma kaka maa ɔne ye bɛda; ɔte musue.
24“Nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ ɛhemɔ anu biala begua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ, ofikyɛ maen maen bɔ méfoa bɛ méfi ɛmɔ nyunu ne, ɔnate sɔ yɔleɛ hemɔ aso yeɛ beguale bɛ nwo fiɛ ɔ, 25Efiɛ hane aseɛ ne, maa yiti nduale ye amumuyɛɛ so kerɛ, na mmane aseɛ ne pole so mmenia. 26Nakoso ɛmɔ de, ɛ́mɔli m’ahyɛdeɛ ne me nhyehyɛleɛ so, na nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ sɔ akyiwadeɛ nemɔ anu biala, kuromani oo, anaa ɛwɔfoɛ bɔ waatena ɛmɔ nu oo. 27(Ofikyɛ aseɛ ne aso ama bɔ né bɛwɔ berɛ koraka yeɛ ɛmɔba ne, sɔ akyiwadeɛ hemɔ amukoraa yeɛ bɛyɔle ɔ, yiti efiɛ hane aseɛ ne.) 28Sɛ ɛmɔfa efiɛ bɛka aseɛ ne a, AWURADE kɔma aseɛ ne kɔpo ɛmɔ, kyɛbɔ ɔmane aseɛ ne pole maen bɔ né bɛte so daa ne. 29Ofikyɛ ebiala bɔ ɔkɔyɔ akyiwadeɛ hemɔ anu biala ne, odi kyɛ bɛpɛ ye asue befi maen ne anu. 30Ɛ́mɔli m’ahyɛdeɛ so, na mmenia bɔ né bɛte aseɛ ne aso daa ne, akyiwadeɛ bɔ bɛyɔle ne, nnɛma ɛmɔyɔ bie, ná ɔnate so ɛmɔangua ɛmɔ nwo fiɛ: Me ole AWURADE ɛmɔ Nyameɛ.”

english_text:
Moral and Religious Laws
1The Lord told Moses 2 to say to the community of Israel:
I am the Lord your God. I am holy, and you must be holy too! 3-4 Respect your father and your mother, honor the Sabbath, and don't make idols or images. I am the Lord your God.
5When you offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, be sure to follow my instructions. 6You may eat the meat either on the day of the sacrifice or on the next day, but you must burn anything left over on the third day. 7If you eat any of it on the third day, the sacrifice will be disgusting to me, and I will reject it. 8In fact, you will be punished for not respecting what I say is holy, and you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
9 When you harvest your grain, always leave some of it standing along the edges of your fields and don't pick up what falls on the ground. 10Don't strip your grapevines clean or gather the grapes that fall off the vines. Leave them for the poor and for those foreigners who live among you. I am the Lord your God.
11 Do not steal or tell lies or cheat others.
12 Do not misuse my name by making promises you don't intend to keep. I am the Lord your God.
13 Do not steal anything or cheat anyone, and don't fail to pay your workers at the end of each day.
14 I am the Lord your God, and I command you not to make fun of the deaf or to cause a blind person to stumble.
15 Be fair, no matter who is on trial—don't favor either the poor or the rich.
16Don't be a gossip, but never hesitate to speak up in court, especially if your testimony can save someone's life.
17 Don't hold grudges. On the other hand, it's wrong not to correct someone who needs correcting. 18 Don't be angry or try to take revenge. I am the Lord, and I command you to love others as much as you love yourself.
19 Breed your livestock animals only with animals of the same kind, and don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field or wear clothes made of different kinds of material.
