5Sɛ eburo afunum nya ɛserɛ ná odi a, aso osũ?
Yeɛ sɛ nandwie koso nya aleɛ a, aso osũ?
6Aleɛ bɔ ɔte bitaa ne, ngyee nne nu a, aso bedi a odi?
Kyiremvua si fufue ne, aso ɔyɛ fɛ?
7Me komvi nne sɔ aleɛ nemɔ aso,
bɛte aleɛ bɔ bɛma me noa nu sa ɔ.
8“O, m’abisadeɛ ne, sɛ ahaa me sa ka ye a,
m’anyelasoɛ ne, sɛ Nyameɛ maa menya ye a,
9sɛ ahaa Nyameɛ kohuro kyɛ okohu me a,
sɛ ahaa ɔkɔte me ngoa nyamaa nu kohũ me a!
10Ahaa ewue ne kɔyɛ m’aworakyekyerɛ,
bɔ m’amaneɛnwunɛ nu po, ahaa me nye kɔgye ɔ,
ofikyɛ Krongronniɛ ne, ye noa dwirɛ ne, nndwi mmvale so.
11M’anwoserɛ wɔ ni, bɔ odi kyɛ megyina so menya anyelasoɛ ɔ?
Yeɛ m’ayieleɛ koyie me sɛ, bɔ odi kyɛ megyina so mekyekye me wora ɔ?
12M’anwoserɛ ne, aso ɔte kyɛ nyɔboɛ anwoserɛ anaa?
Me nwonaen ne, aso ɔte kɔɔbere anaa?
13Nahorɛ nu, mengora ye noa gyina ko,
yeɛ mmokalɛ biala mvi neka fee mma.
14“Sona bɔ wali amia ne, sɛ obiɛngo annwu ye anwumvoin a,
ye de né obiɛngo ne apo kyɛ okosuro Ɛdangama Nyameɛ ɔ.
15Nniɛma mɔ, bedi ngasi kyɛ asue ba bɔ ɔtengyɛ asuso mmerɛ ngome ɔ,
bɛte kyɛ asueba bɔ ɔwewe ɔ,
16bɔ asukɔtwea akata ye nye,
bɔ asue ne ɔtengyɛ wɔ ye bo ɔ.
17Nakoso sɛ ahuhuro mmerɛ ba a, ohuro,
yeɛ sɛ eyia bɔ gyireingyirein a, ye boso mini.
18Dwadifoɛ bɔ bɛtete afupɔngɔ so ne, bɛmakye befi b’atee so,
na bɛkɔ ɛserɛ so bekowuwu.
19Tema dwadifoɛ bɔ bɛtete afupɔngɔ so ne, bɛpena sɔ asueba ne,
Hyeba ateetulɛfoɛ bɛ nye la so kyɛ bekonwu ye ɔ.
20B’aba nu buli, ofikyɛ né bɛ nye la so kyɛ bekonwu ye,
bɛkɔ bekodwu berɛ a, né bɛ nyunu agua ase.
21Sɔ ala yeɛ kekesaala ye ɛmɔ koso ɛmɔmmoka me ɔ;
ɛmɔanwu amaneɛ bɔ wato me ɔ, na wama ɛserɛ aha ɛmɔ.
22Mahã kyɛ mepena akyɛdeɛ mefi ɛmɔ berɛ anaa,
anaakyɛ ɛmɔfa ɛmɔ sikaa betua fea-ase-ma bele me anaa,
23anaakyɛ ɛ́mɔle me befi pɔfoɛ ne sa nu anaa,
anaakyɛ ɛmɔpɔ me befi bɔ ɔteetee me ne sa nu anaa?
24“Ɛmɔhyirehyire me e, na ngomua me noa,
bɔ mayɔ bɔ ɔtte mayee ne, ɛ́mɔma nwu ye.
25Edwirɛ nahorɛ ye hanɛ yɛ se!
Nakoso me nyunu bɔ ɛmɔtwi ye, nzikyɛ paa yeɛ okyire ɔ?
26Me dwirɛ deɛ ne, ɛmɔbu ye animtia hɔ ɔ?
Ɛmɔdwene kyɛ sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ne,
odwudwo gua mvrama nu anaa?
27Ayisiaaniɛ po, ɛmɔgua ye nwo serewa,
yeɛ ɛmɔ adamvo koso, ɛmɔdi ye noa bɛtɔne ye.
28“Afei de, mepena kyɛ ɛmɔnea me nyunu,
ofikyɛ mengɔpɛ anoanu wɔ ɛmɔ nyunu.
29Ɛ́mɔyakyi, nnɛma ɛmɔbua me ndɛengyea,
ɛ́mɔyakyi, na medi be.
30Aso nnakannaka dwirɛ wɔ me noa nu anaa,
anaakyɛ mende yealɛ anaa?

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
Yob bɔ somoɛ
1“Aseɛ ye aso bɔ dasaniɛ te ye,
aso nna nzɔhwɛ serɛserɛ noa yeɛ ogyi ɔ?
Ye ngyẽa ne, aso onzoma paaniɛ ngyẽa.
2Ɔte kyɛ kanganiɛ bɔ ɔpena fɔnwoo nu tena ɔ,
ɔte kyɛ paaniɛ bɔ ɔnwondɛ ye akatuaa ɔ.
3Yiti bosome pee yeɛ nningyein ayɛ basaa wɔ m’asetena nu ɔ,
ɔne aworabɔlɛ kɔngɔen mɔ yeɛ bakyekye basoa me ɔ.
4Sɛ mekɔ meda a, mebisa me nwo kyɛ,
‘Mmerɛ beni koraa yeɛ aleɛ kɔhye maa ngodwɔso ɔ?’
Nakoso aleɛ ngye le,
metɔ faen biribra, né matɔ faen biribra toonn ama aleɛ ahye.
5Me nwonaen alɔ nnɔboakoma, na wayɛ fiɛ betɔɔ,
me wereɛ apakyepakye, na otwi nzue.
6 Me mmerɛ se kɔ ndɛndɛ tra akurokurowa,
na ɔba ayieleɛ bɔ anyelasoɛ biala nne nu ɔ.
7“Kaye kyɛ me ngoa te mvrama,
me nye ngɔgye ko.
8Anyeɛ bɔ onwu me ne, ongonwu me ko,
wɔ nye kotua me, nakoso né matu mamini.
9Na kyɛbɔ munungum se kɔ ná otu mini ne,
sɔ ala yeɛ ebiala bɔ ɔkɔ ɛborɔ dɔ ne, onza mma ko ɔ.
10Onza mma ye awuro berɛ ko,
na nekaa bɔ ɔte ne, berɛ ama ngonwu ye ko.
11“Yiti mengomua me noa,
ngɔhã yealɛ bɔ me sunzum onwu ye ɔ,
na ngɔbɔ aworabɔlɛ bɔ me kra di ɔ nwo somoɛ.
12Aso nde ɛpo anaa ɛpo nu sasrabɔnzam,
bɔ ɛma awɛmvoɛ bɛ nye li me si ɔ?
13Sɛ mesusu kyɛ, ‘Me mba kɔkyekye me wora,
yeɛ me bɛen kɔma me nwo kɔtɔ me kãa a,
14né afa laleɛ anwunanwuna me,
né afa nyekyire aha me serɛ.
15Ah! me kra kuro kyɛ bekomia me kɔme maa ngowu mmom
tra kyɛ ngɔfɔ maa ɔkɔha me mmowue ɔ.
16Afei de, ewiase afono me. Mengɔtena ngoa nu daa.
Yakyi me, ofikyɛ me ngoa te mbaen.
17 Dasaniɛ te nzu koraa, bɔ ebu ye titire sɔa ye,
bɔ w’adwene wɔ ye so sɔa ye,
18bɔ ɛkɔpasa ye nwo ngyerɛmɔ biala ɔ,
bɔ mmerɛ biala eso ye nea enwu kyɛbɔ osi te ɔ?
19Wɔ nye bɔ ɛfa nea me ye, kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛkɔye kofi me so ɔ,
bɔ ɛnyakyi me ma mennya bua nu nzue menza menno po ye?
20Wɔ bɔ esisa adasa ɔ, sɛ mayɔ bɔne po a,
ahaa ɔfa wɔ nwo nzu?
Nzu ati yeɛ atu wɔ nye asie me so ɔ?
Nzu ati yeɛ amaa mayɛ wɔ so tɔsom ɔ?
21Me mmeraatolɛ ne, nzu ati yeɛ ɛmva ngyɛ me ɔ?
M’amumuyɛɛ ne, nzu ati yeɛ ɛnyakyi ma ɔnga ɔ?
Ɔngɔhyɛ biala, ngɔɔla nnɛterɛ nu,
ɛkɔpena me, nakoso né nne berɛ ko.”

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Bildade noa dwirɛ bɔ oli moa
1Yeɛ Suhiniɛ Bildade buale kyɛ,
2“Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛkɔkeka sɔ dwirɛ hemɔ maa okoodwu ɔ,
bɔ ekodwudwo kogua mvrama nu mbaen ɔ?
3Aso Nyameɛ obua ndɛengyea,
anaa Tuminiɛ ne, aso obua ndɛen mundumundu so?
4Sɛ wɔ mma nemɔ bɛyɔle ye bɔne a,
wamaa banya bɛ mmeraatolɛ nwo akatuaa.
5Sɛ ɛkɔpena Nyameɛ si atee,
ná ɛkɔsrɛ Tuminiɛ ne maa okonwu wɔ anwumvoin a,
6sɛ wɔ nwo te ná ɛtengyɛ a,
susu amba kyɛ, ɔkɔkanyane ye nwo ɔkɔboka wɔ,
na ɔkɔma wɔ sa kɔha bɔ ahwere biala.
7Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ɛhyɛle ye bo kaaba bie de,
nakoso w’ayieleɛ nu kɔyɛ piri paa.
8“Bɔ daa ama mɔ baha bato berɛ ne, bisa tie,
ná bɔ bɛ nana mɔ baneanea nu banwu ye ne, dwene ye nwo.
9Yɛ de, anomasi wa ala yeɛ bɛwo yɛ ɔ,
na yɛnze huu,
ofikyɛ aseɛ ye aso, yɛ ngoa otu mini te kyɛ wawoɛ.
10Aso bengohyirehyire wɔ ná baha bahyire wɔ,
aso bɛngɔhã bɛ ti anu nworɛ dwirɛ bengohyire wɔ anaa?
11“Aso elemmire kɔhora kofifi nekaa bɔ asaa nne berɛ ɔ?
Aso ngyɛngyɛma kɔhora konyi nekaa bɔ nzue nne berɛ ɔ?
12Mmerɛ bɔ ɔte frɔmfrɔm bɔ bennya bɛppɛle ne,
bɛkese ndɛndɛ bɛtra ndire biala.
13Ebiala bɔ ɔma ye wora fi Nyameɛ ne, sɔ yeɛ oyie ye ɔ,
na sona bɔ onzuro Nyameɛ ne, ye anyelasoɛ tu mini.
14Bɔ wafa ye nwo wato so ne, ɔsɛkye,
yeɛ ye anyelasoɛ koso ɔyɛ mmerɛ kyɛ ananze ndendaen.
15Ɔfa ye nwo kisa ye sua, nakoso sua ne dwiri gua,
yeɛ ɔfa ye nwo mata sua ne, nakoso sua ne ngora gyina.
16Sɔ sona ne te kyɛ bakaa bɔ onyi frɔmfrɔm wɔ eyia nu ɔ,
na ye mmaen nemɔ nu trɛtrɛ wɔ eboo ne anu.
17Ye ndii mendamenda nyɔboɛ nyɔboɛ,
na nyɔboɛ nyɔboɛ nemɔ afia yeɛ owura ɔ.
18Sɛ betu ye befi ye boso a,
ye boso berɛ nekaa bɔ ogyi ne ɔpo ye,
na ose ye kyɛ, ‘Wɔ de, nnwuni wɔ le.’
19Yoo, ye anigye atee bɔ ɔnate so ɛne,
na mmakaa foforɛ koso fifi wɔ ye boso berɛ.
20“Daabi, sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ ne, Nyameɛ mbo ye,
yeɛ ɔmmoka bɔnefoɛ.
21Ɔkɔmaa ɛkɔseresere bieku,
ná wama wɔ noa ali ahurusi.
22Animguaseɛ kɔmata wɔ pɔfoɛ mɔ,
na amumuyɛɛfoɛ awuro kɔbɔ tɔɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Yob ma Bildade mmuayɛɛ
1Yeɛ Yob mane mmuayɛɛ kyɛ,
2 “Nahorɛ nu, mese kyɛ ɔte sɔ,
nakoso ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né dasaniɛ watengyɛ wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu?
3Sɛ ebie kuro kyɛ ɔne ye bɛbɔ kuro a,
edwirɛ apee ko bɔ Nyameɛ kobisa ne, ɔngɔhora nu ko po noa ye.
4Ye nworɛ ne ye tumi te totohyia,
nwa yeɛ wadwɔso watia ye bɔ wafa ye nwo wali tɔtorɔtɔɔ ɔ?
5Ye bɔ otutu mmokaa bo gua bɔ ɔmmɔ bɛ kɔkɔ ɔ,
ye bɔ ɔfɛ yaa dwiri bɛ gua ɔ,
6ye bɔ ɔwoso aseɛ fi ye boso,
ná ɔma aseɛ nyinasoɛ mɔ bɛwoso ɔ.
7Ye bɔ ɔhyɛ eyia kyɛ nnɛmaa opukye a ombukye ɔ,
ye bɔ omundu nzramaa mɔ nyunu mma bɛ nda ɔ.
8Ye bɔ ye ngome yeɛ ɔtrɛtrɛle ewienu nu ɔ,
ye bɔ otiatia ɛpo asorɔkye so ɔ.
9 Ye bɔ ɔyɔle nzramaa kure bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu sorɔ, ɔne ewienu afia,
Akɔtaen-ne-ye-mma,
yeɛ nzramaa kure bɔ ɔwɔ ewienu ngwaen.
10Ye bɔ ɔyɔ nningyein mbiri mbiri bɔ ɔbo sona ndeaseɛ so ɔ,
anwanwadeɛ bɔ ɛka a ennwu ye noa ɔ.
11Eh, ɔpɛ nu me nwo wa, nakoso mennwu ye;
ɔsẽ kɔ, nakoso me nye mbɛ ye so.
12Sɛ ofoti nikyee kɔ a, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kosi ye atee ɔ?
Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kobisa ye kyɛ, ‘Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛ́yɔ e?’
13“Nyameɛ ngɔhwe ye yaafɛlɛ ne ngosa,
na bɛ bɔ bɛboka Rahabo ne,
Nyameɛ abrɛ bɛ ase maa bawura ye bɔbɔ ye bo.
14Yiti, me ole nwa bɔ mekora meye me noa mekyire ye ɔ,
anaa, ngɔyɛ sɛɛ né mahora masa me nwo mahyire ye?
15Sɛ medi be po a, mengɔhora ngɔye me noa ngohyire ye,
na mmom ngɔsrɛ me ndɛenbualɛniɛ ne, kyɛ onwu me anwumvoin.
16Sɛ mefrɛ ye ndɛenbualɛniɛ nyunu ná ɔba a,
menne menni kyɛ bɔ meka ye ɔkɔtɛ me so ɔ.
17Ofikyɛ ɔnate edwirɛ kãa bie ati opura me,
na ɔma me nwo yɛ ngena ngena bɔ nnyɛle hwee ɔ.
18Ɔmma menne me nwome,
na mmom waprapra aworabɔlɛ wagua me so.
19Sɛ ɔba kyɛ yɛli ye anwoserɛ so a, ye yeɛ ɔte anwoserɛniɛ ɔ!
Yeɛ sɛ ɔba ndɛenbualɛ koso a, ndɛenbualɛniɛ beni nyunu yeɛ ɔkɔhɔ ɔ?
20Sɛ medi be po a, ahaa me bɔbɔ me noa kobua me fɔ,
yeɛ sɛ mvomsoɛ nne me nwo po a, ɔkɔmaa ngonwu kyɛ me dwirɛ nyɛ fɛ.
21Mvomsoɛ biala nne me nwo de, nakoso menze me bɔbɔ me nwo yé;
afei de, ewiase afono me.
22Ye mukoraa pɛ; na ɛhe ati yeɛ menwa:
bɔ mvomsoɛ nne ye nwo oo,
bɔ ɔte amumuyɛɛniɛ oo,
ode bɛ mukoraa bɛ ngoa fi bɛ sa nu.
23Sɛ asane si ma mmenia wuwu mvum nu a,
mmenia bɔ bedi be ne, b’amaneɛnwunɛ ɔyɛ ye sere.
24Wafa aseɛ wawura bɔnefoɛ sa,
ɔma nu ndɛenbualɛfoɛ bebu bɛ nye begua nahorɛ so.
Sɛ nna ye ahɔ a, né nzaade nwa ɔ?
25“Me ngyẽa ɔsẽ kɔ ndɛndɛ tra sona bɔ otu amirika ɔ,
me ngyẽa ɔnwati kɔ bɔ mennwu anika biala wɔ me nu ɔ.
26Ɔpɛ nu kɔ ndɛndɛ kyɛ ɛlɛen bɔ ɔla asue nye ɔ,
ɔkɔ ndɛndɛ kyɛ kɔleɛ bɔ ɔto kye naen ɔ.
27Sɛ meka kyɛ, ‘Ngɔma me wora kofi somoɛ bɔ mebɔ ne,
ngɔyakyi me nyunu bɔ mayɛ ye aworabɔlɛ aworabɔlɛ ne,
ná mama me nye agye’ a,
28né m’amaneɛnwunɛ ne amukoraa afa ɛserɛ wato me so,
ofikyɛ mese kyɛ engobua me be.
29Na sɛ ekobua me fɔ a,
nzu ati yeɛ meha me nwo mbaen ɔ?
30Sɛ mefa nzue gyengɔgyengɔ mebia,
ná mefa kondu menwunzi me sa po a,
31ekofindi me kɔto kumaa pikapika nu,
na me nwo kɔyɛ me bɔbɔ me ndaadeɛ po tɛ.
32Ofikyɛ ye de, ɔtte dasaniɛ kyɛ me,
ná mahora masa me nwo mahyire ye,
ná yahora yagyina yabɔ nguro.
33Ndɛenbualɛniɛ biala nne berɛ bɔ ogyi yɛ afia,
bɔ okoli yɛ munyɔ yɛ afia dwirɛ ɔ.
34Sɛ ɔye amaneɛ bɔ wafa wato me so ne ofi me so,
ná wamma ye nwo suronyi wandɔ me so a,
35ye de mengɔfa ye nwo suronyi yeɛ ngodwudwo ɔ,
ofikyɛ me de, mese kyɛ nna sɔ yeɛ nde ɔ.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
Ewiase afono me
1“Ewiase afono me,
afei de, ngɔhã edwirɛ bɔ ɔha me ɔ,
edwirɛ yealɛ bɔ ɔwɔ me nu ne, ngɔhã.
2Ngɔhã ngohyire Nyameɛ kyɛ, ‘Nnɛbua me fɔ.
Maa nwu nikyee bɔ yiti yeɛ afa wɔ dwirɛ ateta me e.
3Aso ɔte paa ma wɔ kyɛ ɛkɔfa me kɔfa ateetee nu ɔ,
kyɛ ɛkɔpo wɔ sa noa adwuma ɔ,
ɔne kyɛ ɛkɔma wɔ nye kɔgye amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɛ porɛbɔlɛ nwo ɔ?
4Aso kuro sona anyeɛ yeɛ ele ye ɔ?
Kyɛbɔ sona nwu nikyee ne, aso sɔ yeɛ enwu ye ɔ?
5Wɔ ngoa ngyẽa, ye somaa ne, ɔte kyɛ sona deɛ anaa?
Anaa wɔ ngoa afoɛ, ye somaa ne, ɔte kyɛ sona deɛ anaa;
6bɔ me nwo mvomsoɛ yeɛ ɛneanea nu ɛpena ɔ,
ɔne kyɛ me bɔne yeɛ ɛfeefee nu ɛpena ɔ?
7Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ɛse kyɛ menni fɔ,
yeɛ ebiala koso nne berɛ bɔ okole me kofi wɔ sa nu ɔ.
8Wɔ sa yeɛ ɔnwone me yɔle me ɔ,
nakoso apɛ wɔ nwo esa ku me.
9 Kaye kyɛ ɛfale nnɛterɛ yeɛ ɛnwone me ɔ;
na ɛkɔmaa ngosa ngɔkakyi nnɛterɛ anaa?
10Aso amma manyɛ kyɛ nyɔfonesue bɔ wala ɔ,
ɔne nyɔfonesue bɔ babɔ ye kunguma ɔ?
11Ɛfale wereɛ ne anwoɔnaen edwirale me nwo,
yeɛ ɛfale mmowue ne ndii ɛpombale me sosɔle so.
12Ama me ngoa,
yeɛ aye ɔdɔ pindinn ali ahyire me,
na ɛnealɛ bɔ ɛnea me so ne yeɛ ɔbɔ me sunzum nwo waen ɔ.
13Nakoso afa sɔ dwirɛ nemɔ asie maa wayɛ wɔ mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ,
na manwu kyɛ porɛ bɔ ɛbɔle hɔ ɛhe:
14Ɛtetɛ me nea sɛ aso ngɔyɔ bɔne a,
na ɛngɔfa me nwo ngɔhyɛ me wɔ me mvomsoɛ nwo.
15Sɛ meyɔ amumuyɛɛ a, ye de me yaakɔ!
Yeɛ sɛ meyɔ bɔ ɔtengyɛ po a, mengɔhora me ti so ma,
ofikyɛ me nwo yɛ me nya,
yeɛ matɔ amaneɛ nu.
16Sɛ mema me nwo so a,
ɛyɛ kyɛ gyata bɔ ye nye aboro ɔ ɛfoa me,
na esa yɔ anwanwadeɛ nningyein etia me.
17Ɛfa amaneɛ foforɛ to me so maa ɔyɛ adanzeɛ tia me,
ɛfɛ me nwo yaa piri paa,
na ɛfa ɛlɔen foforɛ ɛba me so.
18 “Ao! Nzu ati yeɛ ɛmaa me ni wole me ɔ?
Sɛ nwuli koraka yeɛ bɛ nye pɛ me so a, ahaa ɔte paa.
19Ahaa nyɛle kyɛ nikyee bie bɔ ɔnne berɛ koraa ɔ!
Mvili me ni akunu ne, ahaa beesiele me berɛ ala.
20Aso me ngoa ɔtte tikaape bie? Ma ye bo ɔpɛ.
Yakyi me maa me wora kyekye kãa,
21koraka né mahɔ nekaa bɔ mengosa ngɔwa ko ɔ,
koraka né mahɔ awosii tunn ne awosii kabii maen ne anu,
22awosii tunn ne basabasa maen ne,
bɔ berɛ kanea te kyɛ awosii ne.”

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Sofa noa dwirɛ bɔ oli moa
1Yeɛ Naamaniɛ Sofa buale kyɛ,
2“Edwudwolɛ worawora ne, aso onni kyɛ mebua ye nwo bie anaa?
Sɛ sona dwudwo worawora a, né okyire kyɛ odi be anaa?
3Wɔ dwudwolɛ mbaen mbaen ne, ɔkɔmaa mmenia komua bɛ noa anaa?
Sɛ ɛgoro ebie nwo a, aso ebie wora ongogua wɔ nyunu ase anaa?
4Ofikyɛ ɛnwa: ‘Me ngyerɛkyerɛ te sannwuu,
na me nwo te wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu.’
5Nakoso, ao, sɛ ahaa Nyameɛ dwudwole a,
sɛ ahaa obukyele ye noa hane edwirɛ hyirele wɔ a,
6ahaa ɔkɔha nworɛ nwo mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ kohyire wɔ,
ofikyɛ nworɛ gua ahoroɔ pee.
Nwu ye kyɛ, wɔ mvomsoɛ nwo asohwenɛ bɔ anya ye ne,
Nyameɛ abu ye nye wagua mvomsoɛ ne bie aso.
7“Nyameɛ mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ ne, ɛkɔhora kɔte ye bo?
Tuminiɛ ne, ɛkɔhora kɔte ye bo koyie bɔkɔɔ?
8Ye nworɛ ne, ye konguronn tra nyameɛso. Ɛyɛ sɛɛ né ate ye bo?
Ye kuronn tra ɛborɔ. Ɛyɛ sɛɛ né anwu sɔ nworɛ ne?
9Ye tendenn nu tra aseɛ,
yeɛ ye tɛtrɛtɛɛ nu tra ɛpo.
10Sɛ ɔba ná ɔfa mmenia gua kuku nu,
ná ɔfa mmenia kɔ nekaa bɔ bedi dwirɛ a,
nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kosi ye ate ɔ?
11Ofikyɛ ye de ɔse mmenia bɔ benni nahorɛ ɔ,
na sɛ onwu bɔne wɔ sona nwo a,
aso okobu ye nye kogua so?
12Nakoso anzana kwaseambane konwu nworɛ ne,
sana eburo afunum wawo sona koraka.
13“Sɛ ɛma wɔ bra yɛ sannwuu a,
yeɛ ɛkɔfa w’abisadeɛ ɛkɔto ye nyunu ɔ.
14Sɛ bɔne wɔ wɔ nu a, yakyi ye yɔlɛ korakorakora,
yeɛ nnɛma amumuyɛɛ tena w’awuro.
15Ɔba ye sɔ a, ɛkɔpagya wɔ ti
bɔ wɔ tiboa ngobua wɔ fɔ ɔ,
ekogyina pirim, na engosuro.
16Ofikyɛ, wɔ wora kofi w’aworabɔlɛ,
na ɛkɔkaye ye kyɛ nzue bɔ wasẽ wahɔ ɔ.
17Wɔ ngoa kɔta hyireinn kɔtra eyia ketee,
na ye awosii po ɔkɔyɛ kyɛ ngyerɛmɔ.
18Ekogyina pindinn, ofikyɛ anyelasoɛ wɔ berɛ,
ɔkɔbɔ wɔ nwo waen, na ɛkɔla asomdwee nu.
19Ɛkɔla bɔ ebiala ngonwunanwuna wɔ ɔ,
na mmeni pee kɔpena mmokalɛ kofi wɔ berɛ.
20Nakoso amumuyɛɛfoɛ de, bɛ nye so kɔyɛ bɛ wusiwusi,
bengonya neka fee bɛngɔnwati ngɔhɔ,
na b’anyelasoɛ ala ole ewue.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
16just as he rules over liars
and those they lie to.
17God shames counselors,
turns judges into fools,
18and makes slaves of kings.
19God removes priests and others
who have great power—
20he confuses wise,
experienced advisors,
21puts mighty kings to shame,
and takes away their power.
22God turns darkness to light;
23he makes nations strong,
then shatters their strength.
24God strikes their rulers senseless,
then leaves them to roam
through barren deserts,
25lost in the dark, staggering
like someone drunk.
translation_text:
Yob ma bɛ mmuayɛɛ
1Yeɛ Yob buale kyɛ,
2“Ɔnyɛ nwanwa! Ɛmɔ yeɛ mmenia noa dwirɛ tua ɛmɔ noa ɔ,
na ɛmɔwu a, né nworɛ bo apɛ.
3Nakoso me wora, adwene wɔ me ti anu kyɛ ɛmɔ ala,
ɛmɔ nworɛ ndra me deɛ.
Nwa ala yeɛ ɔnze edwirɛ hemɔ ɔ?
4Me nwo yɛ me mmango mɔ sere,
me bɔ mesu mefrɛ Nyameɛ a ɔma me mmuayɛɛ ɔ,
sona bɔ metengyɛ, bɔ mvomsoɛ nne me nwo
yeɛ me nwo yɛ mmenia sere ye.
5Bɛ bɔ bɛ so anu atɔ bɛ ne,
bebu bɛ bɔ amaneɛ ato bɛ ɔ animtia,
na amaneɛ asiesie ye nwo ɔnwondɛ bɛ bɔ basoti ɔ.
6Nakoso ɛhawo ɔnne awerɔm awuefoɛ b’awuro,
yeɛ bɛ bɔ bewura Nyameɛ apue ne koso, banya asomdwee,
eh, aso bɛ yeɛ Nyameɛ maa oyie bɛ yé ɔ?
7“Nakoso, bisa ngaka mɔ, na bekohyirehyire wɔ,
bisa ewienu nnomaa, na bɛkɔhã bekohyire wɔ.
8Bisa aseɛ so mmakaa, na bekohyirehyire wɔ,
bisa ɛpo nu naen, na bɛkɔhã bekohyire wɔ.
9Bɛ mukoraa bɛ nu beni yeɛ ɔnze ɔ,
kyɛ AWURADE yeɛ wayɔ sɔ nikyee ne ɔ?
10Abɔdeɛ biala bɔ ole ngoa ne, ye sa nu yeɛ ye ngoa wura ɔ,
yeɛ ye sa nu yeɛ sona biala ye nwomeɛ wura ɔ.
11Aso asoɛ nde nzonzoleɛ bɔ ɔwɔ edwirɛ nu,
kyɛbɔ temverema koso tafe aleɛ nea ne?
12 Mbanyi mɔ berɛ yeɛ nworɛ wɔ ɔ,
yeɛ ndeaseɛ koso wɔ bɛ bɔ banyi bahyɛ ɔ berɛ.
13“Nyameɛ berɛ yeɛ nworɛ ne tumi wɔ ɔ,
ye berɛ yeɛ foɛtulɛ ne ndeaseɛ wɔ ɔ.
14Sɛ odwiri nikyee gua a, ebiala ngɔhora ngosa ngosi,
sɛ ɔto sona kuku nu a, ebiala ngɔhora ye bukye.
15Tie, sɛ ɔma esue yakyi tɔlɛ a, wawa pe wɔ aseɛ so,
yeɛ sɛ ɔma esue tɔ koso a, nzue bu fa aseɛ so.
16Ye berɛ yeɛ anwoserɛ ne nworɛ wɔ ɔ,
sona bɔ bɛlakalaka ye ne, ɔne nnakannakaniɛ ne,
bɛ munyɔ bewura ye bo.
17Ɔma foɛtulɛfoɛ bɛ nworɛ fi bɛ ti anu,
yeɛ ɔma ndɛenbualɛfoɛ bɛyɛ ngwaseaa.
18Ɔsangye ahemvo mɔ b’abɔsoɛ nu,
na ɔfa nyamaa ɔbɔ bɛ abɔsoɛ.
19Opuro asɔfo mɔ bɛ ndaadeɛ,
na otu tumifoɛ fi bia so.
20Mmenia bɔ bɛ noa ate ne, ɔma bɛ noa mua,
na ode mbanyi mɔ bɛ nimdeɛ fi bɛ sa.
21Ɔma mmenia bu atitirefoɛ animtia,
na ogoho anwoserɛfoɛ b’abɔsoɛ nu.
22Obukye mvealeɛ nu dwirɛ bɔ ɔfea awosii nu so,
na ɔma awosii kabii kakyi hyireinn.
23Ɔma maen mɔ so, yeɛ osa bɔ bɛ,
ɔma maen mɔ trɛ, na osa maa bɛbɔ aya.
24Mbanyi bɔ bɛla mmenia noa wɔ aseɛ so ne, ode bɛ nworɛ fi bɛ sa nu,
na ɔmaa bemini bekyinikyini ɛserɛ bɔ atee nne so ɔ so.
25Befuafua awosii bɔ kanea nne nu ɔ nu,
na ɔmaa bɛnate fofalifofali kyɛ akɔnomnzaniɛ.

english_text:
Job Continues
I Know and Understand
1I know and understand
every bit of this.
2None of you are smarter
than I am;
there's nothing you know
that I don't.
3But I prefer to argue my case
with God All-Powerful—
4you are merely useless doctors,
who treat me with lies.
5The wisest thing you can do
is to keep quiet 6and listen
to my argument.
7Are you telling lies for God
8and not telling the whole truth
when you argue his case?
9If he took you to court,
could you fool him,
just as you fool others?
10If you were secretly unfair,
he would correct you,
11and his glorious splendor
would make you terrified.
12Your wisdom and arguments
will blow away like dust.
Be Quiet While I Speak
13Be quiet while I speak,
and we'll see what happens.
14I will be responsible
for what happens to me.
15God may kill me, but still
I will trust him
and offer my defense.
16This may be what saves me,
because no guilty person
would come to his court.
17Listen carefully to my words!
18I have prepared my case well,
and I am certain to win.
19If you can prove me guilty,
I will give up and die.
Job Prays
I Ask Only Two Things
20I ask only two things
of you, my God,
and I will no longer
hide from you—
21stop punishing
and terrifying me!
22Then speak, and I will reply;
or else let me speak,
and you reply.
23Please point out my sins,
so I will know them.
24Why have you turned your back
and count me your enemy?
25Do you really enjoy
frightening a fallen leaf?
26Why do you accuse me
of horrible crimes
and make me pay for sins
I did in my youth?
27 You have tied my feet down
and keep me surrounded;
28I am rotting away like cloth
eaten by worms.
translation_text:
Yob toa so dwudwo
1“Tie, ɛhe amukoraa me nye anwu ye,
yeɛ me so ate, na mate ye bo.
2Bɔ ɛmɔse ne, me koso mese,
ɛmɔ nworɛ ndra me deɛ.
3Me de, Tuminiɛ ne mmom yeɛ mepena kyɛ me ne ye yɛdwudwo ɔ,
Nyameɛ yeɛ mepena kyɛ me ne ye yɛbɔ kuro ɔ.
4Na ɛmɔ de, ɛmɔ noa nu yeɛ ɛmɔbobɔ ɔ,
ɛmɔ amukoraa bɛte safoɛ bɔ mvasoɛ nne ɛmɔ so ɔ.
5Sɛ ɛmɔmua ɛmɔ noa mmom a,
ahaa okyire kyɛ ɛmɔse nworɛ!
6Mesrɛ ɛmɔ, ɛ́mɔtie me kurobɔlɛ ne,
ná ɛmɔyɛ asoɛ betie bɔ meka mefa meye me noa ɔ.
7Aso Nyameɛ yeɛ ɛmɔgyi ye gya nu bɛka ngondombo dwirɛ ye?
Ye yeɛ ɛmɔgyi ye gya nu bɛka nnakannaka dwirɛ ye?
8Aso ɛmɔgyi Nyameɛ si anaa,
anaakyɛ ɛmɔka bie bɛma ye?
9Sɛ ɔneanea ɛmɔ nu a, aso ɛmɔ nwo kɔyɛ sannwuu?
Anaakyɛ, ɛmɔkɔhora bɛkɔlakalaka ye kyɛbɔ sona lakalaka sona anaa?
10Nahorɛ nu, sɛ ɛmɔfea ɛmɔ nwo bɛka bie bɛma ye a,
okohwi ɛmɔ nyunu.
11Ye tumi totohyia ne, aso ɔngɔma ɛmɔngosuro?
Ye nwo suronyi ne, aso ɔngɔtɔ ɛmɔ so?
12Ɛmɔ anyandera ne, yɛte ye daa, mvasoɛ nne so,
yeɛ ɛmɔ kurobɔlɛ ne koso, ɔndɔ asoɛ nu.
13“Ɛ́mɔma nya me so, ná ndwudwo,
bɔ ɔkɔto me biala, maa ɔto me!
14Nzu ɔ? Ngɔyɔ bɔ ɔkɔma me ti kɔkeka ɔ,
ngɔfa me ngoa ngɔto serewa.
15Sɛ oku me po a, ye yeɛ ɔte m’anyelasoɛ ɔ,
nakoso me ne ye yɛkɔbɔ kuro.
16Na ɛhe yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ me ngoalelɛ ɔ,
ofikyɛ amumuyɛɛniɛ biala ngogyina ye nyunu.
17Ɛ́mɔyɛ asoɛ betie me dwirɛ ye yé,
ná edwirɛ bɔ meka mefa mesa me nwo ne, ɛ́mɔma ɔhɔ ɛmɔ so anu.
18Me dwirɛ ne, madwene ye nwo masie,
na mese kyɛ me nwo kofi.
19Nwa yeɛ ɔne me yɛbaabɔ kuro ɔ?
Ahaa ye de ngomua me noa ná mawu.
Yob bisa Nyameɛ pena bɔne bɔ wayɔ ɔ
20Oo Nyameɛ, nikyee nyɔ pɛ yeɛ mebisa mefi wɔ berɛ ɔ,
ɔba ye sɔ a, mengɔfa me nwo ngɔfea wɔ:
21Amaneɛ bɔ afa ato me so ne, ye fi me so,
yeɛ nnɛma wɔ nwo suronyi ɔtɔ me so.
22Na afei, to wɔ sa frɛ me, na ngɔye me noa,
anaakyɛ maa mmɔ me kuro ma ɛye ye noa.
23Me mvomsoɛ ne me bɔne, ye somaa te nyɛɛ?
Maa nwu me mmeraatolɛ ne me bɔne.
24Nzu ati yeɛ afa wɔ nyunu afea me e,
bɔ afa me ayɛ wɔ pɔfoɛ ye?
25Nyaa bɔ mvrama bɔ ye kɔ ɔ, aso ekonwunanwuna ye?
Aso ɛkɔfoa ɛserɛ worowaa?
26Ofikyɛ edwirɛ tɛɛ yeɛ ɛkyerɛ tia me ɔ,
na ɛfa me mmerandeɛ nu bɔne nwo akatuaa etua me so kerɛ.
27 Ɛbɔ me panwu,
ɛfa wɔ nye sra agyirɛ biala bɔ metu ɔ,
na ato wɛen afa nekaa bɔ odi kyɛ me gya tia ɔ.
28Sona de, ɔte kyɛ dufure, ɔporɔ,
na ɔtete kyɛ ɛtena bɔ mvrɔlɔ ali ɔ.

english_text:
Job Continues His Prayer
Life Is Short and Sorrowful
1 Life is short and sorrowful
for every living soul.
2We are flowers that fade
and shadows that vanish.
3And so, I ask you, God,
why pick on me?
4There's no way a human
can be completely pure.
5Our time on earth is brief;
the number of our days
is already decided by you.
6Why don't you leave us alone
and let us find some happiness
while we toil and labor?
When a Tree Is Chopped Down
7When a tree is chopped down,
there is always the hope
that it will sprout again.
8Its roots and stump may rot,
9but at the touch of water,
it sprouts once again.
10Humans are different—
we die, and that's the end.
11We are like streams and lakes
after the water has gone;
12we fall into the sleep of death,
never to rise again,
until the sky disappears.
13Please hide me, God,
deep in the ground—
and when you are angry no more,
remember to rescue me.
Will We Humans Live Again?
14Will we humans live again?
I would gladly suffer
and wait for my time.
15My Creator, you would want me;
you would call out,
and I would answer.
16You would take care of me,
but not count my sins—
17you would put them in a bag,
tie it tight,
and toss them away.
18But in the real world,
mountains tumble,
and rocks crumble;
19streams wear away stones
and wash away soil.
And you destroy our hopes!
20You change the way we look,
then send us away,
wiped out forever.
21We never live to know
if our children are praised
or disgraced.
22We feel no pain but our own,
and when we mourn,
it's only for ourselves.
translation_text:
Sona ngoa te tika
1“Dasaniɛ bɔ brasua awo ye ɔ,
ye ngoa te tika, na amaneɛ ngome.
2Opukye kyɛ bakaa nyerɛen, na ɔkese,
ɔpɛ nu kɔ kyɛ wawoɛ, na ɔngyɛ né watu wamini.
3Aso ɛhe yeɛ ama wɔ nye ali ye si ye,
bɔ afrɛ me awa wɔ nyunu, kyɛ ɛbaabua me ndɛen ye?
4Nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora konya bɔ ye nwo te okofi bɔ ye nwo nde ɔ nu ɔ?
Ebiala ngɔhora!
5Ɔnate kyɛ, ye ngoa bɔ okonya ye ne, ahyehyɛ ye tendenn ato berɛ,
ɔne bosome somaa bɔ okonya ye ɔ ato berɛ,
yeɛ apɛ ɛwɛen ato berɛ bɔ ɔngɔhora ye tra ɔ ne ati,
6nzaade yakyi ye ma ye nwo ɔtɔ ye e,
kyɛbɔ paaniɛ yie ye adwuma a,
ole anigye ɔnwondɛ kyɛ okonya ye ɛlɛho akatuaa ɔ.
7“Ofikyɛ bakaa po, anyelasoɛ wɔ berɛ ma ye,
kyɛ bɛpɛ ye bɛto a, okosa kɔfefɛ,
na okosa konya nyaa foforɛ.
8Ye ndii nemɔ, ɔwɔ nu kyɛ betwindwam wɔ aseɛ ne abo dɔ de,
yeɛ ye dosii ne koso owu aseɛnwo berɛ de,
9nakoso sɛ onya nzue kaala pɛ a, ɔfefɛ,
na ɔyeye mmaen kyɛ bakaa bɔ batu batɛ ɔ.
10Nakoso dasaniɛ de, owu a, ɔda berɛ bɔ ɔngekã ye nwo ɔ,
sɛ sona ka nu a, né ɔwɔ nisua?
11Kyɛbɔ ɛkwaa nu nzue wewe,
ná asue koso otu ɔbɔ mvuture ne,
12sɔ ala yeɛ dasaniɛ da berɛ, bɔ ondwɔso ko ɔ.
Na anwuro onnya ɔppɛle nu ye de, bengotingye,
yeɛ bengotingye bɛ ngofi bɛ nnaa nu.
13Oo, me ngome a, ahaa afa me afea wɔ ɛborɔ,
ahaa afa me asie kɔpem kyɛ w’ahone kɔtɔ nzue nu ɔ,
ahaa ahyɛ mmerɛ bɔ medi ye wɔ ɛborɔ dɔ ɔ, ná akaye me.
14Sɛ dasaniɛ wu a, ɔkɔtena ngoa nu bieku anaa?
Koɛ noa bɔ ngyi wɔ m’asetena nu ye, ngɔnwondɛ,
kɔpem kyɛ ngɔpɔno ngole me nwome ɔ.
15Ɛkɔfrɛ me, na ngosuro wɔ so,
na wɔ wora kɔlɔ wɔ sa noa adwuma ne.
16Afei, ɛkɔfa wɔ nye kɔsra m’agyirɛ biala bɔ ngotu ɔ,
na mmom ɛngɔtetɛ me ngɔnea me bɔne.
17Ekowura me mmeraatolɛ kotoku nu kɔkyekye ye noa,
na ɛkɔkata me bɔne so.
18“Nakoso, kyɛbɔ bokaa dwiri gua ase ɔnyoko,
ná nyɔbotaen tu fi ye boso,
19ná asue twi fa nyɔboɛ nwo maa ohi,
ná asue yi pia aseɛnwo nnɛterɛ kɔ ne,
sɔ ala yeɛ ɛma dasaniɛ anyelasoɛ otu mini ɔ.
20Edi ye so tumi afebɔɔ, na ewue fa ye kɔ,
ɛma ye nyunu sesã bɔ onzoma ye ɔ, na ede ye ngoa fi ye sa nu.
21Sɛ ye mma mɔ benya animnyam po a, ɔnze,
yeɛ sɛ mmenia gua bɛ nyunu ase koso a, onnwu ye.
22Ye bɔbɔ ye nwonaen nu yealɛ angome yeɛ ɔte ɔ,
na ye kra sũ ye bɔbɔ ye nwo.”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Second Speech
If You Had Any Sense
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
* 2Job, if you had any sense,
3you would stop spreading
all of this hot air.
4Your words are enough
to make others turn from God
and lead them to doubt.
5And your sinful, scheming mind
is the source of all you say.
6I am not here as your judge;
your own words are witnesses
against you.
7Were you the first human?
Are you older than the hills?
8Have you ever been present
when God's council meets?
Do you alone have wisdom?
9Do you know and understand
something we don't?
10We have the benefit of wisdom
older than your father.
11And you have been offered
comforting words from God.
Isn't this enough?
12Your emotions are out of control,
making you look fierce;
13that's why you attack God
with everything you say.
14 No human is pure and innocent,
15and neither are angels—
not in the sight of God.
If God doesn't trust his angels,
16what chance do humans have?
We are so terribly evil
that we thirst for sin.
Just Listen to What I Know
17Just listen to what I know,
and you will learn
18wisdom known by others
since ancient times.
19Those who gained such insights
also gained the land,
and they were not influenced
by foreign teachings.
20But suffering is in store
each day for those who sin.
21Even in times of success,
they constantly hear
the threat of doom.
22Darkness, despair, and death
are their destiny.
23They scrounge around for food,
all the while dreading
the approaching darkness.
24They are overcome with despair,
like frightened soldiers facing
a fearsome king in battle.
25This is because they rebelled
against God All-Powerful
26and have attacked him
with their weapons.
27They may be rich and fat,
28but they will live in the ruins
of deserted towns.
29Their property and wealth
will shrink and disappear.
30They won't escape the darkness,
and the blazing breath of God
will set their future aflame.
* 31They have put their trust
in something worthless;
now they will become worthless
32like a date palm tree
without a leaf.
33Or like vineyards or orchards
whose blossoms and unripe fruit
drop to the ground.
34Yes, the godless and the greedy
will have nothing but flames
feasting on their homes,
35because they are the parents
of trouble and vicious lies.
translation_text:
Elifase noa dwirɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ
(15.1—21.34)
1Yeɛ Temanniɛ Elifase buale kyɛ,
2“Aso ɔsɛ kyɛ nworɛniɛ ɔfa nimdeɛ huuhuu ɔye dwirɛ noa,
ná ɔfa edwirɛ bɔ aba nne nu ɔ ɔhoahoa ye nwo?
3Aso odi kyɛ osu edwirɛ mbaen mbaen nwo aporowaa,
ná ɔkekã edwirɛ bɔ mvasoɛ nne so anaa?
4Ama Nyameɛ nwo surolɛ afi wɔ nu,
na ɛmaa ɔyɛ se ma wɔ kyɛ ɛkɔbɔ mbaeɛ kohyire Nyameɛ ɔ.
5Ofikyɛ wɔ bɔne yeɛ okyire wɔ edwirɛ bɔ ɛkeka ɔ,
na nnakannakafoɛ dwirɛ yeɛ ɛkã ɔ.
6Wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ noa dwirɛ yeɛ obua wɔ fɔ ɔ, na mmom nna me ɔ,
amba, wɔ noa dwudwolɛ yeɛ odi adanzeɛ tia wɔ ɔ.
7“Aso wɔ yeɛ ɛte kuro sona bɔ belili moa bɛwole wɔ ɔ?
Bɛwole wɔ koraka yeɛ bɛbɔ mmokaa ɔ?
8Nyameɛ mvealeɛ nu nhyehyɛleɛ ne, atie nu dwirɛ?
Wɔ ngome yeɛ ɛse nworɛ ɔ?
9Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛse bɔ yɛ de yɛnze ɔ?
Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɛte ye bo bɔ yɛ de yɛnde ye bo ɔ?
10Nea, bɛ bɔ bafu gyein, ɔne bɛ bɔ banyi paa ɔ bɛwɔ yɛ nu,
bɔ banyi batra wɔ baba po ɔ.
11Nyameɛ aworakyekyerɛ dwirɛ ne,
ɔne ye akorɔkorɔ dwirɛ ne,
aso ebu ye kyɛ ɔte nikyee ba bie anaa?
12Nzu ati yeɛ ɛpe dwirɛ nwo sɔa ye?
Nzu ati yeɛ ama wɔ nye aboro ɔ,
13bɔ ɔnate so ama w’ahone ahu Nyameɛ so,
bɔ ama sɔ dwirɛ ne afite wɔ noa ɔ?
14 Dasaniɛ ole nwa bɔ ye nwo kora te ɔ?
Sona beni yeɛ brasua awo ye bɔ ɔtengyɛ ɔ?
15Tie, Nyameɛ ye krongronfoɛ po, ɔmva ye nwo ndo bɛ so,
yeɛ anwuro po ye nwo nde wɔ ye nye so.
16Né nzaade busueniɛ bɔ ye suban aporɔ,
bɔ wafa amumuyɛɛ wayɛ ye nzue ne, ogyi ye sɛ!
17“Ngohyirehyire nu ngohyire wɔ, na tie me,
bɔ manwu ye ne yeɛ ngɔhã ngohyire wɔ ɔ.
18Ɔte edwirɛ bɔ nworɛfoɛ baha bato berɛ,
bɔ bɛ nana mɔ bamva banzie bɛ,
19bɔ bɛ nana mɔ ngome yeɛ Nyameɛ fale aseɛ ne mane bɛ ɔ,
bɔ ɛwɔfoɛ biala wambɛ nu wɔ bɛ berɛ ɔ.
20Bɔnefoɛ nwo ndɔ ye wɔ mmerɛ biala bɔ ɔte ase ɔ,
na sɔ ala yeɛ ebiala bɔ ye ti anu te awosii ne,
ɔte ma ye wɔ mmerɛ biala bɔ ɔte ase ɔ.
21Ahunundetelɛ ma ye so anu ndɔ ye,
na ye asomdwee mmerɛ nu po, sɛkyefoɛ ne ba ye so.
22Onne nni kyɛ okosa kofi awosii nu ɔ,
na ye ayieleɛ ole ngrandɛ noa.
23Okyinikyini pena aleɛ, na obisa kyɛ, ‘Nisua yeɛ aleɛ wɔ ɔ?’
Na ɔse kyɛ ɔngɔhyɛ né awosii kyẽa ato ye.
24Aworabɔlɛ ne ahunundetelɛ nwunanwuna ye,
na bɛba ye so kyɛ ɛhene bɔ waboaboa ye nwo ɔkɔ koɛ ɔ.
25Ofikyɛ watengyɛ ye sa Nyameɛ nyunu,
na wadwɔso watia Tuminiɛ ne.
26Otira akokyɛm kubuu,
bɔ wayɛ ye nwo lɔen wafa wahɔ ye so ɔ.
27Na ɔnate kyɛ ye nyunu ayɛ twotwofii,
ná ye mvenu koso ayɛ twotwofii ne ati,
28ɔkɔtena kurofoen so,
ɔne awuro bɔ wakakyi dandue,
bɔ bahyehyɛ bato berɛ kyɛ okobu kogua ɔ.
29Ongonya ye nwo, ye anwonya ne ngɔhyɛ,
na ye anwonya ngotira ndii wɔ aseɛ so.
30Ongofi awosii nu ngofite le,
ɔkɔyɛ kyɛ bakaa, see kɔyera ye nyaa,
na mvrama kohu ye nyerɛen ne kɔhɔ.
31Nnɛmaa ɔfa ye nwo to nningyein bɔ mvasoɛ nne so ɔ so ɔlakalaka ye nwo,
ofikyɛ nningyein bɔ mvasoɛ nne so ɔ yeɛ ɔkɔyɛ ye akatuaa ɔ.
32Ye sa kɔha ye akatuaa koraka né wawu,
na ɔkɔyɛ kyɛ bakaa nyaa bɔ wakese bɔ ɔngɔyɛ monɛ ɔ.
33Ɔkɔporo ye mma amui kogua kyɛbɔ bobe bakaa yɔ ne ala,
yeɛ ɔkɔwoso ye nyerɛen kogua kyɛbɔ olive bakaa yɔ ne ala.
34Ofikyɛ amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɛ boso konua,
na see kɔyera sua bɔ bafa fea-ase-ma basi ɔ.
35Bɛnwonzɛ nzɛmmɔne, na bɛwo musue,
na nnakannaka ayi b’ahone nu.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
I Have Often Heard This
1Job said:
2I have often heard this,
and it offers no comfort.
3So why don't you keep quiet?
What's bothering you?
4If I were in your place,
it would be easy to criticize
or to give advice.
5But I would offer hope
and comfort instead.
6If I speak, or if I don't,
I hurt all the same.
My torment continues.
7God has worn me down
and destroyed my family;
8my shriveled up skin proves
that I am his prisoner.
9God is my hateful enemy,
glaring at me and attacking
with his sharp teeth.
10Everyone is against me;
they sneer and slap my face.
11And God is the one
who handed me over
to this merciless mob.
Everything Was Going Well
12Everything was going well,
until God grabbed my neck
and shook me to pieces.
God set me up as the target
13for his arrows,
and without showing mercy,
he slashed my stomach open,
spilling out my insides.
14God never stops attacking,
15and so, in my sorrow
I dress in sackcloth
and sit in the dust.
16My face is red with tears,
and dark shadows
circle my eyes,
17though I am not violent,
and my prayers are sincere.
18If I should die,
I beg the earth not to cover
my cry for justice.
19 Even now, God in heaven
is both my witness
and my protector.
20My friends have rejected me,
but God is the one I beg
21to show that I am right,
just as a friend should.
22Because in only a few years,
I will be dead and gone.
translation_text:
Yob gyi ye gya nu kyɛ odi be
1Yeɛ Yob buale kyɛ,
2“Edwirɛ sɔaa mɔ de, mate pee,
ɛmɔ amukoraa bayɛ kyɛ ɛmɔdodo me,
nakoso ɛmɔgoro me nwo!
3Ɛmɔ noa dwirɛ mbaen mbaen ne, kyinzu yeɛ ye bo kɔpɛ ɔ?
Nzikyɛ yeɛ ɔha wɔ ɔ, bɔ yiti ɛtɛ dwudwo ye?
4Tebea bɔ nwɔ nu ye, sɛ nu yeɛ ɛmɔ wɔ a,
ahaa me koso ngɔhora ngodwudwo kyɛ ɛmɔ ala;
ahaa ngɔhora ngodwudwo worɔworɔ ngogua ɛmɔ so,
ná masere ɛmɔ.
5Ahaa ngɔfa me noa dwirɛ ngɔhyɛ ɛmɔ nguraen,
ahaa me noa dwudwolɛ kɔma ɛmɔ nwo tutulɛ ne kɔtɔ ɛmɔ.
6“Sɛ medwudwo a, me nwo tutulɛ ne ndɔ me,
yeɛ sɛ mandɛ me noa nu koso a,
nzikyɛ yakyilɛ yeɛ me nwo tutulɛ ne yakyi ɔ?
7Amba, Nyameɛ amaa madwɔso me sonaluwaa so,
wanua me nwo ama amukoraa bɛ boso.
8Wama me nwonaen atwindwam,
bɔ ɔte adanzeɛ tia me ɔ;
na ɛfɔen bɔ mafɔ ne odwɔso tia me,
ɔte adanzeɛ tia me.
9Okyi me, na wafɛ yaa watete me nu pasapasa,
wanwose ye gye wahyire me,
me pɔfoɛ ne henahena ye nye kyire me.
10Batu bɛ noa bagua me so,
babobɔ me so anu bagoro me nwo,
na bɛboa bɛ noa bɛko betia me.
11Nyameɛ afa me wawura busuefoɛ mɔ sa,
na wasumu me wato nzɛmmɔnefoɛ bɛ sa nu.
12Ahaa né me nwo atɔ me, nakoso wabu me nu gyein,
obumane me kɔme, na ɔtetele me nu pasapasa;
na watu ye nye wasie me so.
13Ye agyaentolɛfoɛ bapɛ me nwo bayia,
ɔpakyepakye me saa nu bɔ onnwu me anwumvoin ɔ,
na otu m’abɔwee gua ase.
14Ebubulɛ ala yeɛ obubu me ɔ,
na ɔba me so kyɛ koɛhonɛniɛ.
15Mapa ɛsɛen tena mahera,
na magyi m’anwoserɛ mato asefuo nu.
16Esuɛ ama me nyunu ayɛ yurohaa,
na me nye asi apini wayɛ awosii tunn.
17Nakoso nnyɔle nzɛmmɔne biala,
yeɛ me mbaeɛ nwo koso te.
18“Oo aseɛ, nnɛkata me mogya so,
nnɛma me sufrɛ ne ye bo pɛ.
19 Na kekesaala ye po, tie, m’adanzeniɛ wɔ nyameɛso,
yeɛ bɔ ɔka bie ma me ne koso ɔwɔ anwuro.
20Me damvo mɔ po bɛgoro me nwo,
nakoso Nyameɛ yeɛ meporo moen mekyire ye ɔ,
21kyɛ okoli sona ne Nyameɛ b’afia dwirɛ ɔ,
kyɛbɔ sona di obiɛngo ti dwirɛ ɔ.
22Ofikyɛ waha m’afoɛ kãa bie,
né mahɔ nekaa bɔ bɛkɔ a benza bɛmma ɔ.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
My Hopes Have Died
1My hopes have died,
my time is up,
and the grave is ready.
2All I can see are angry crowds,
making fun of me.
3If you, Lord, don't help,
who will pay the price
for my release?
4My friends won't really listen,
all because of you,
and so you must be the one
to prove them wrong.
5They have condemned me,
just to benefit themselves;
now blind their children.
6You, God, are the reason
I am insulted and spit on.
7I am almost blind with grief;
my body is a mere shadow.
8People who are truly good
would feel so alarmed,
that they would become angry
with my worthless friends.
9They would do the right thing
and because they did,
they would grow stronger.
10But none of my friends
show any sense.
11My life is drawing to an end;
hope has disappeared.
12But all my friends can do
is offer empty hopes.
13I could tell the world below
to prepare me a bed.
14Then I could greet the grave
as my father
and say to the worms,
“Hello, mother and sisters!”
15But what kind of hope is that?
16Will it keep me company
in the world of the dead?
translation_text:
1Me kra nwo ato, ewue apingye me,
asieleɛ la berɛ ɔnwondɛ me.
2Susu amba kyɛ, ngorohoɛfoɛ bapɛ me nwo bayia,
na me nye tua ngorohoɛ bɔ bɛgoro me nwo ɔ.
3“Gyina me gya nu fa wɔ bɔbɔ wɔ nwo si awowaa;
nwa yeɛ okoli me agyinamuɛ ɔ?
4Ato b’adwene nu ama bɛ ndeaseɛ abɔ bɛ,
yiti ɛngɔma bengoli ngonim.
5Ebiala bɔ ɔye ye damvo mɔ ma,
maa ɔnate so onya b’agyapadeɛ nu kyɛfa ne,
sɔ bɔne ne nwo akatuaa kɔwa ye mma so.
6“Wamaa mayɛ mmenia bɛ noa nu ngorohoɛ dwirɛ,
na makakyi sona bɔ mmenia tiatia ye nyunu ɔ.
7Aworabɔlɛ ama me nye mmaa apakye,
na madwɔso me sonaluwaa so mayɛ kyɛ wawoɛ.
8Mmenia bɔ bɛtengyɛ ne, benwu me a, bɛ nwo dwiri bɛ,
na sona bɔ odi be ne, ɔfɛ amumuyɛɛniɛ so yaa.
9Nakoso sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ de, ye atee so yeɛ ɔnate ɔ,
yeɛ bɛ bɔ bɛ bra te sannwuu ne, bɛkɔ so benya anwoserɛ.
10Nakoso ɛmɔ amukoraa, ɛ́mɔhã bɔ ɛmɔkekã ne bieku,
na mengonwu nworɛniɛ ko po wɔ ɛmɔ nu.
11Ewue apingye me; me nzusuleɛ ayɛ mbaen,
yeɛ bɔ ɔla m’ahone nwo bɔ mepena ne koso, wayɛ mbaen.
12Bɛfa alesaleɛ bɛkakyi alehyeleɛ,
bɛka kyɛ, ‘Ɔngɔhyɛ né wata hyireinn, wɔ aberɛ bɔ awosii awa ɔ.’
13Sɛ me nye la so kyɛ ɛborɔ kɔyɛ m’awuro,
sɛ meto me mba wɔ awosii nu,
14ná mekã mekyire asieleɛ kumaa kyɛ, ‘Me se ole wɔ,’
ɔne nnɔboakoma kyɛ, ‘Me ni ne nniɛma brasua ole wɔ’ a,
15né m’anyelasoɛ wɔ ni?
Nwa yeɛ okonwu m’anyelasoɛ ne ɔ?
16M’anyelasoɛ ne, aso ɔne me koowura ɛborɔ dɔ pambim ne anu?
Aso yɛkɔbɔ nu yɛkɔhɔ mvuture nu?

english_text:
Bildad's Second Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk?
Be sensible! Let us speak.
3Or do you think that we
are dumb animals?
4You cut yourself in anger.
Will that shake the earth
or even move the rocks?
* 5 The lamps of sinful people
soon are snuffed out,
6leaving their tents dark.
7Their powerful legs become weak,
and they stumble on schemes
of their own doing.
* 8Before they know it,
9they are trapped in a net,
10hidden along the path.
11Terror strikes and pursues
from every side.
12Starving, they run,
only to meet disaster,
13then afterwards to be eaten alive
by death itself.
14Those sinners are dragged
from the safety of their tents
to die a gruesome death.
15Then their tents and possessions
are burned to ashes,
16and they are left like trees,
dried up from the roots.
17They are gone and forgotten,
18thrown far from the light
into a world of darkness,
19without any children
to carry on their name.
20Everyone, from east to west,
is overwhelmed with horror.
21Such is the fate of sinners
and their families
who don't know God.
translation_text:
Bildade noa dwirɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ
1Yeɛ Suhiniɛ Bildade buale kyɛ,
2“Kyinzu yeɛ ɛmɔkɔyakyi edwirɛ mbaen mbaen ne kekanɛ ɔ?
Ɛ́mɔfa bɛhɔ adwenedwene nu, ná afei yɛtoa so yɛdwudwo.
3Nzu ati yeɛ ebu yɛ kyɛ yɛte ngaka ɔ?
Nzu ati yeɛ ebu yɛ kyɛ adwene nne yɛ ti anu ɔ?
4Wɔ bɔ wɔ yaafɛlɛ amaa atete pasapasa ɔ.
Ɔnate wɔ ti odi kyɛ mmenia tu fi aseɛ so anaa,
anaakyɛ odi kyɛ betutu nyɔbotaen mɔ befi bɛ boso anaa?
5 “Nahorɛ nu, amumuyɛɛniɛ kanea nua,
na ye see te mosonomosono.
6Ye awuro kanea kakyi awosii,
na ye kanea bɔ osinze berɛ ne koso nua.
7Ye natelɛ nu anwoserɛ noa kɔbrɛ ase,
na ye bɔbɔ ye porɛ bɔ ɔbɔ ɔ yeɛ ofi ye ase ɔ.
8Ofikyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye gya diedie ye kowura ngaen nu,
na otutu ye gya kɔtɔ kumaa nu.
9Kafoli kɔsɔ ye gya ndii nu,
ná tukɔ ahye ye asie berɛ.
10Bɛkɔbɔ kɔtɔkaa bɛkɔfea aseɛnwo bɛkɔnwondɛ ye,
na bekosua ye ngaen wɔ atee so.
11Ahunundetelɛ kɔtɔ ye so wɔ nekaa biala,
na ahunundetelɛ kɔfoa ye koli ye si.
12Ɛhɔen kɔma ye anwoserɛ koyie,
na musue asiesie ye nwo kyɛ ɔkɔmaa okosoti.
13Anwonyerɛ didi ye nwonaen,
na ewue anwonyerɛ suronyisuronyi didi ye gya ne ye sa.
14Ye awuro bɔ ɔte ye anyelasoɛ ne, betu ye befi nu,
na bɛtwe ye bɛkɔ ɛhene atianuserɛniɛ ne nyunu.
15Ebiala kora tena nu, ofikyɛ nna ye awuro ahɔ ko,
na bɛfa sɔfe bɛpetepete berɛ.
16Ye ndii twindwam wɔ aseɛnwo,
na ye mmaen koso kese wɔ anwuro.
17Ye nwo ngayeɛ komini kofi aseɛ ye aso,
na ebiala ngɔkaye ye dumaa wɔ aseɛ ye aso le.
18Befindi ye befi nekaa bɔ ɔte hyireinn nu bɛto awosii nu,
na betu ye befi wiase.
19Ongonya mmaa anaa ye bosofoɛ wɔ ye abusua nu,
na nekaa bɔ né ɔte daa ne,
ebiala ngonya ye ti ngodidi nu.
20Edwirɛ bɔ ɔkɔto ye ne, ɔkɔma eyia atɔleɛfoɛ bɛ nwo kodwiri bɛ,
na ɛserɛ kɔha eyia afiteleɛfoɛ.
21Nahorɛ nu, sɔ yeɛ amumuyɛɛfoɛ b’ayieleɛ yie bɛ ɔ,
na bɛ bɔ bɛnze Nyameɛ ne, bɔ ɔto bɛ hɔ ala ɛne.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
How Long Will You Torture Me?
1Job said:
2How long will you torture me
with your words?
3Isn't ten times enough
for you to accuse me?
Aren't you ashamed?
4Even if I have sinned,
you haven't been harmed.
5You boast of your goodness,
claiming I am suffering
because I am guilty.
6But God is the one at fault
for finding fault with me.
7Though I pray to be rescued
from this torment,
no whisper of justice
answers me.
8God has me trapped
with a wall of darkness
9and stripped of respect.
10God rips me apart,
uproots my hopes,
11and attacks with fierce anger,
as though I were his enemy.
12His entire army advances,
then surrounds my tent.
I Am Forgotten
* 13God has turned relatives
and friends against me,
14and I am forgotten.
15My guests and my servants
consider me a stranger,
16and when I call my servants,
they pay no attention.
17My breath disgusts my wife;
everyone in my family
turns away.
18Young children can't stand me,
and when I come near,
they make fun.
19 My best friends and loved ones
have turned from me.
20I am skin and bones—
just barely alive.
21My friends, I beg you for pity!
God has made me his target.
22Hasn't he already done enough?
Why do you join the attack?
23I wish that my words
could be written down
24or chiseled into rock.
25I know that my Protector lives,
and at the end
he will stand on this earth.
26My flesh may be destroyed,
yet from this body
I will see God.
27Yes, I will see him for myself,
and I long for that moment.
28My friends, you think up ways
to blame and torment me, saying
I brought it on myself.
29But watch out for the judgment,
when God will punish you!
translation_text:
Yob kɔ so nya Nyameɛ nu gyidie
1Yeɛ Yob buale kyɛ,
2“Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛmɔkɔyakyi me halɛ ɔ?
Kyinzu koraa yeɛ ɛmɔkɔyakyi edwirɛ bɔ ɛmɔka bɛteetee me ye ɔ?
3Pɛen buru mumua ɛhe yeɛ ɛmɔadwudwo batia me ɔ,
aso ɔnyɛ ɛmɔ nya kyɛ ɛmɔmaa mefa yealɛ nu ɔ?
4Na sɛ ɔte nahorɛ po kyɛ mayɔ mvomsoɛ a,
me mvomsoɛ mata me.
5Susu amba kyɛ, sɛ ɛmɔdwene kyɛ ɛmɔte paa bɛtra me,
ná ɛmɔbu m’amaneɛnwunɛ ne kyɛ ɔte me bɔne nwo adanzeɛ a,
6ye de memaa ɛmɔnwu ye kyɛ, Nyameɛ yeɛ wama ɛhe ato me ɔ,
na wagua ye asawu wahye me.
7Na sɛ metea nu kyɛ, ‘Ebie le me oo!’ a, ebiala ndɛ me so,
yeɛ metea nu mepena mmokalɛ koso a, ebiala nga bie mma me.
8Wayɔ aberedwaa wafa me nwo, bɔ mengora menze mengɔ ɔ,
na wama m’atee so ayɛ awosii.
9Wale m’animnyam wafi me sa nu,
na watu m’anidie abotire ne.
10Wabubu me nekaa biala, bɔ afei de nnde sona ko ɔ,
na watu m’anyelasoɛ bo kyɛ bakaa.
11Wama ye ahone ahu me so,
na obu me ye pɔfoɛ.
12Ye lɔen bɛbɔ nu bɛba me so,
baye atee bɔ bɛfa so bɛba me so ɔ,
na bakyekye asikyeleɛ bapɛ me tena sua nwo bayia.
13“Wate nniɛma mɔ wafi me nwo maa baali dedeede,
na wamaa mayɛ ɛwɔfoɛ wɔ me manifoɛ mɔ nu.
14M’abusuafoɛ bayakyi me nu bahɔ,
mmiɛngo paa mɔ bɛ wora afi me.
15Bɛ bɔ masikye bɛ wɔ m’awuro ne, bɛ wora afi me;
m’afaneɛ mɔ bebu me kyɛ nde wɔfoɛ,
na makakyi bɛ nye so amanvraniɛ bie.
16Mefrɛ me somvoɛ a, ɔndɛ me so,
sana mebukye me noa mesrɛ ye koraka.
17Me ye po, me nwomeɛ bo ye,
na me kunu mmaa po, bɛmbena me nyunu bɛnnea.
18Ngwadaa mmaa mmaa po, bebu me animtia,
na sɛ meyɛ kyɛ menatenate a, né bɛgoro me nwo.
19Me nwo yɛ me damvo paa mɔ amukoraa ahi,
yeɛ mmenia bɔ mekuro bɛ dwirɛ ne koso,
bapɛ bɛ nwo bɛko betia me.
20Me nwo ayeye mmowue mmowue,
na mawu mayie, bɔ ewue li me mvanvando ɔ.
21Ao, me damvo mɔ, ɛ́mɔnwu me anwumvoin e,
ɛ́mɔnwu me anwumvoin e,
ofikyɛ Nyameɛ ate ye sa wapura me!
22Nzu ɔ ɛmɔatu bɛ nye basie me so,
kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ atu ye nye wasie me so ye?
Bɔ wayɛ me nwonaen ye, aso ɔnha ɛmɔ?
23“O, sɛ ahaa bɛkyerɛ me dwirɛ ne a!
Sɛ ahaa bɛkyerɛ begua nwomaa nu a!
24Sɛ ahaa bɛfa buralɛ pɛn, ɔne sum
bekolikoli begua nyɔboɛ so maa ɔtena berɛ afebɔɔ a!
25Ofikyɛ me de, mese kyɛ me Defoɛ ne ɔte ase,
na ayieleɛ ne, okoli me dwirɛ kɔma me wɔ aseɛ ye aso.
26Na sɛ anwonyerɛ didi me wereɛ sɛkye ye yie a,
ndɛ wɔ anwoɔnaen nu ye de, ngonwu Nyameɛ.
27Ye bɔ me bɔbɔ ngonwu ye,
me nye konwu ye ɔ,
ná ɔngɔyɛ me nye so wɔfoɛ ɔ.
Me wora dɔ kyɛ sɔ mmerɛ ne kodwu!
28Sɛ ɛmɔka kyɛ, ‘Yɛkɔyɔ sɛɛ né yatane ye nye?’
ɔne kyɛ, ‘Amaneɛ bɔ onwu ye ne, ofi ye bɔbɔ’ a,
29ye de odi kyɛ ɛmɔsuro ngrandɛ ne,
ofikyɛ ɛyaafɛlɛ ne kɔmaa ɛmɔkonwu ngrandɛ noa asohwenɛ,
na ɛhe kɔma ɛmɔkonwu kyɛ ndɛenbualɛ wɔ berɛ.”

english_text:
Zophar's Second Speech
Your Words Are Disturbing
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2Your words are disturbing;
now I must speak.
3You have accused
and insulted me,
and reason requires a reply.
4Since the time of creation,
everyone has known
5that sinful people are happy
for only a while.
6Though their pride and power
may reach to the sky,
7they will disappear like dust,
and those who knew them
will wonder what happened.
8 They will be forgotten
like a dream
9and vanish from the sight
of family and friends.
10Their children will have to repay
what the parents took
from the poor.
11Indeed, the wicked will die
and go to their graves
in the prime of life.
Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
12Sinners love the taste of sin;
they relish every bite
13and swallow it slowly.
14But their food will turn sour
and poison their stomachs.
15Then God will make them lose
the wealth they gobbled up.
16They will die from the fangs
of poisonous snakes
17and never enjoy rivers flowing
with milk and honey.
18Their hard work will result
in nothing gained,
19because they cheated the poor
and took their homes.
20Greedy people want everything
and are never satisfied.
21But when nothing remains
for them to grab,
they will be nothing.
22Once they have everything,
distress and despair
will strike them down,
23and God will make them swallow
his blazing anger.
24 While running from iron spears,
they will be killed
by arrows of bronze,
25whose shining tips go straight
through their bodies.
They will be trapped by terror,
26and what they treasure most
will be lost in the dark.
God will send flames
to destroy them in their tents
with all their property.
27The heavens and the earth
will testify against them,
28and all their possessions
will be dragged off
when God becomes angry.
29This is what God has decided
for those who are evil.
translation_text:
Sofa noa dwirɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nyɔ
1Afei Naamaniɛ Sofa buale kyɛ,
2“Tie! Edwirɛ ne ha me paa bɔ odi kyɛ mebua ye nwo bie ɔ,
yiti mengonya ye nwo aboterɛ.
3Edwirɛ bɔ mate kyɛ ɛkeka ne, otwi me,
na me ndeaseɛ kanyane me kyɛ mma wɔ mmuayɛɛ.
4Yiti ɛnze kyɛ ofi tetetete,
ofi mmerɛ bɔ Ɛdangama bɔle sona tole aseɛ ye aso ɔ,
5kyɛ bɔnefoɛ ngɔsoɛ ɔndena berɛ ngyɛ,
ɔne kyɛ sona bɔ ɔnze Nyameɛ ne, ye anigye te tikaape bie ɔ?
6Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ɔmoma ye nwo so kodwu anwuro anwuro,
ma ye ti kɔka munungum de,
7nakoso ye boso komini kyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye bondua;
na bɛ bɔ banwu ye ne, bekobisa kyɛ, ‘Ɔwɔ nisua?’
8Okotu komini kyɛ laleɛ, bengonwu ye ko;
ye boso komini kyɛ kɔngɔen nyekyire.
9Anyeɛ bɔ onwuni sɔ sona nen, ongonwu ye ko,
na okotu komini bɔ bengonwu ye wɔ ye awuro ɔ.
10Ye mma mɔ kɔfa mbata kɔma ehiafoɛ,
na ye anwonya bɔ wanya ye ne, okopu kɔwa.
11Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ ye mmerandeɛ nu anwoserɛ ma ye mmowue nu yɛ se de,
nakoso ɔkɔfa kɔhɔ kumaa nu.
12“Ɔwɔ nu kyɛ amumuyɛɛ te ye noa nu menemene,
yeɛ ɔfa fea ye temverema bo de,
13ɔwɔ nu kyɛ onguro kyɛ ɔyakyi nu,
na ɔfa wura ye nnaalɔ de,
14nakoso ye aleɛ dwu ye kunu dɔ a, ɔkakyi yɛ weewee,
na ɔyɛ ɛkyenebene noa borɔ wɔ ye nu.
15Ɔsesa anwonya ɔbɔ so meme, nakoso osa fe bɛ ba,
Nyameɛ tu anwonya ne fi ye kunu dɔ gua.
16Ɔkɔtafe ɛkyenebene borɔ,
na ɛbɔnaa yeɛ ɔkɔha ye kohũ ye ɔ.
17Ye nye ngonwu asue mmaa mmaa mɔ,
ongonwu woɛ ne nyɔfonesue asue bɔ ɔtengyɛ ne.
18Nikyee bɔ wafɛ wanya ye biala,
okopu kɔwa bɔ ɔngɔme ɔ,
na mvasoɛ bɔ okonya kofi ye dwaalilɛ nu ne,
ongonya nu anigye.
19Ofikyɛ wasisi mmenia bɔ bɛyɛ anwumvo ɔ, na wasa wapo bɛ,
na wale sua bɔ nna ye yeɛ osili ɔ mbendene so.
20“Ɔnate kyɛ ɔte adifuu ne ati,
ɔngora mva nikyee bɔ ye nye gye ye nwo ɔ onzie.
21Odidi a, ɔnyakyi bie,
yiti ye anwonya ngosi pasiliwa biala.
22Ye anwonya mmorosoɛ ne asi ne po, ye nwo ngɔtɔ ye,
na musue amukoraa kɔtoto ye.
23Odidi ma ye ko yi pambee.
Nyameɛ kɔfɛ ye so yaa piri paa,
na okohwie ye yaafɛlɛ ne kogua ye so maa ɔkɔkakyi ye aleɛ.
24Sɛ ɔnwati fi buralɛ akodeɛ noa a,
kɔɔbere agyaen kosina ye.
25Agyaen ne sina ye fite,
ye noa ne sina ye abɔwee nu fite,
na ewue nwo suronyi tɔ ye so.
26Basiesie awosii tunn bato berɛ bama ye anwonyadeɛ,
see bɔ nna sona yeɛ ofita nu ɔ yeɛ ɔkɔyera ye ɔ,
na ebiala bɔ waha ye awuro berɛ ne, ɔkɔyera kɔtɔ nzoen.
27Nyameɛso kɔma ye amumuyɛɛ nwo kɔla berɛ,
na aseɛ kodwɔso kotia ye.
28Nzue koyi kɔfa ye awuro agyapadeɛ,
okopia agyapadeɛ ne kɔhɔ wɔ Nyameɛ ɛyaafɛlɛ kyẽa ne.
29Sɔ yeɛ Nyameɛ ma amumuyɛɛniɛ ayieleɛ yie ye ɔ,
agyapadeɛ bɔ Nyameɛ ahyehyɛ wato berɛ wama ye hɔ ɛne.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
If You Want To Offer Comfort
1Job said:
2If you want to offer comfort,
then listen to me.
3And when I have finished,
you can start your insults
all over again.
4My complaint is against God;
that's why I am impatient.
5Just looking at me is enough
to make you sick,
6and the very thought of myself
fills me with disgust.
7Why do evil people live so long
and gain such power?
8Why are they allowed to see
their children grow up?
9They have no worries at home,
and God never punishes them.
10Their cattle have lots of calves
without ever losing one;
11their children play and dance
safely by themselves.
12These people sing and celebrate
to the sound of tambourines,
small harps, and flutes,
13and they are successful,
without a worry,
until the day they die.
Leave Us Alone!
14Those who are evil say
to God All-Powerful,
“Leave us alone! Don't bother us
with your teachings.
15What do we gain from praying
and worshiping you?
16We succeeded all on our own.”
And so, I keep away from them
and their evil schemes.
17How often does God become angry
and send disaster and darkness
to punish sinners?
18How often does he strike them
like a windstorm
that scatters straw?
19You say, “God will punish
those sinners' children
in place of those sinners.”
But I say, “Let him punish
those sinners themselves
until they really feel it.
20Let God All-Powerful force them
to drink their own destruction
from the cup of his anger.
21Because after they are dead,
they won't care what happens
to their children.”
Who Can Tell God What To Do?
22Who can tell God what to do?
He judges powerful rulers.
* 23Some of us die prosperous,
24enjoying good health,
25while others die in poverty,
having known only pain.
26But we all end up dead,
beneath a blanket of worms.
27My friends, I know that you
are plotting against me.
28You ask, “Where is the home
of that important person
who does so much evil?”
29Everyone, near and far, agrees
30that those who do wrong
never suffer disaster,
when God becomes angry.
31No one points out their sin
or punishes them.
32Then at their funerals,
they are highly praised;
33the earth welcomes them home,
while crowds mourn.
34But empty, meaningless words
are the comfort you offer me.
translation_text:
Yob ma Sofa mmuayɛɛ
1Yeɛ Yob buale kyɛ,
2Ɛ́mɔyɛ asoɛ betie me dwirɛ ye yé,
ná ɔyɛ aworakyekyerɛ bɔ ngonya ngofi ɛmɔ berɛ ɔ.
3Ɛ́mɔma me koso ndwudwo bie,
na sɛ medwudwo meyie a, afei né ɛmɔagoro me nwo.
4Me de, aso dasaniɛ yeɛ mebɔ ye somoɛ anaa?
Nzu ati yeɛ ɔnzɛ kyɛ mefɛ yaa ɔ?
5Ɛ́mɔnea tebea bɔ nwɔ nu ɔ, na ɔkɔyɛ ɛmɔ aworabɔ
maa ɛmɔkɔfa ɛmɔ sa bɛkɔsɔ ɛmɔ noa.
6Sɛ medwene ye nwo a, né ɔyɛ me suro,
na ɔma me nwo wosowoso me.
7Nzu ati yeɛ bɔnefoɛ mɔ bɛkɔ so benya ngoa ɔ,
benyi bɛkyɛ, ná bɛkɔ so benya ngɔsoɛ mbiri mbiri ɔ?
8Oyie bɛ mma mɔ yé maa bɛtenatena bɛ nwo,
na oyie bɛ boso ama mɔ yé maa bɛ nye nwu bɛ.
9Asomdwee wɔ b’awuro, bɔ ahunundetelɛ biala nne berɛ ɔ,
yeɛ Nyameɛ asohwenɛ ne bie ɔmma bɛ so.
10Ye nandwie nyii ɔkɔ so wo,
na ye nandwie beleɛ kɔ so wo mmaa, bɔ ɔmbɔ ba ɔ.
11Amumuyɛɛfoɛ mɔ, bɛma bɛ mma mmaa mmaa mɔ
befite bekotu mbasa kyɛ mmoaen kure,
na bɛ mma mɔ huru pepe bedi angorɛ.
12Bɛfa akasaa ne sangoo bɛkenga dwein bɛto,
na behu awɛen bɛma bɛ nye gye.
13Amumuyɛɛfoɛ di bɛ mmerɛ wɔ anwonya nu,
na afei, bɛkɔ ɛborɔ.
14Bɛka bekyire Nyameɛ kyɛ, ‘Fi yɛ so kɔ!
Ofikyɛ yɛmbena kyɛ yɛnya w’atee nwo nimdeɛ biala.
15Tuminiɛ ne te nzu, bɔ ɔsɛ kyɛ yɛso ye ɔ?
Yɛbɔ mbaeɛ yɛkyire ye a, nzikyɛ mvasoɛ yeɛ yɛkonya ɔ?’
16Tie, bɛ ngɔsoɛ ne, aso nna bɛ bɔbɔ bɛ sa nu yeɛ ɔwɔ ɔ?
Mekyi bɔnefoɛ foɛtulɛ kɔkɔkɔkɔ.
17“Nea kyɛbɔ bɔnefoɛ ye kanea ɔtaa nua ɔ!
Nea kyɛbɔ musue taa toto ye ɔ!
Nea kyɛbɔ Nyameɛ osi kyekyɛ aworabɔlɛ wɔ ye yaafɛlɛ nu ɔ!
18Pɛen nyɛɛ yeɛ mvrama ɔbɔ bɛ kɔ kyɛ ɛserɛ ɔ?
Pɛen nyɛɛ yeɛ mvrama piri ɔbɔ bɛ kɔ kyɛ afafu ɔ?
19Ɛmɔnwa: ‘Bɔnefoɛ amumuyɛɛ nwo asohwenɛ ne,
Nyameɛ boaboa ye noa gua berɛ ma ye mma mɔ.’
Na mesrɛ kyɛ, ótua ye bɔbɔ ye kerɛ ma onwu ye.
20Mesrɛ kyɛ ye bɔbɔ ye nye onwu musue bɔ ɔkɔto ye ɔ,
mesrɛ kyɛ onwu amaneɛ wɔ Tuminiɛ ne ye ɛyaafɛlɛ nu.
21Ofikyɛ, sɛ ye ngoa bo pɛ a,
nikyee biala bɔ ɔkɔto ye abusua bɔ wayakyi ye berɛ ne, ɔmva ye nwo.
22Aso ebie kɔhora kohyire Nyameɛ nworɛ,
ye bɔ obua nyameɛsofoɛ ndɛen ɔ?
23Sɛ ebie baawu a, né ɔwɔ anwotɔ tebea nu,
ye so anu tɔ ye, nikye fee nha ye,
24ɔyɛ piri tukutuku,
na ye bowue nu mia.
25Yeɛ ebie wora, ye kra di aworabɔlɛ kɔ ewue nu,
bɔ onnya asetena nu anigye ɔ.
26Nakoso besie bɛ mukoraa wɔ nnɛterɛ nu,
na nnɔboakoma to fa bɛ nwo.
27“Nea, manwu ɛmɔ adwene,
ɔne porɛ bɔ ɛmɔabɔ bafa me nwo ɔ.
28Ofikyɛ ɛmɔnwa: ‘Sona titire ne, ye awuro ne wɔ ni?
Ɛtena sua bɔ amumuyɛɛfoɛ nemɔ bɛtenane nu ne, ɔwɔ ni?’
29Mmenia bɔ bɛfa atee ne aso ne, aso ɛmɔnnya bebbisale bɛ?
Aso ɛmɔnne b’adanzeɛ ne bɛndo nu,
30kyɛ kyẽa bɔ asane kosi ne, amumuyɛɛniɛ onya ye ti didi nu ɔ,
kyɛ ɛyaafɛlɛ kyẽa ne, bɛpepɛ bede ye ɔ?
31Amumuyɛɛniɛ ye bɔne yɔleɛ ne, nwa yeɛ ɔkora fa si ye nyunu ɔ?
Nwa yeɛ otua ye kerɛ wɔ ye bɔne yɔleɛ nwo ɔ?
32Sɛ bekosie ye a,
bɛwɛne ye asieleɛ ne.
33Kumaa nu nnɛterɛ bɔ ɔla nu ne, ɔyɛ ye fɛ,
ebiala di ye si maa bekosie ye,
yeɛ bɛ bɔ beli ye nyunu koso, bɛsone pembepembe.
34Edwirɛ basabasa mbaen he,
ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né ɛmɔahora bafa bakyekye me wora,
wɔ aberɛ bɔ ɛmɔ mmuayɛɛ te ngondombo ngome ɔ?”

english_text:
Eliphaz's Third Speech
What Use Are We Humans to God?
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2 What use are we humans
to God,
even the wisest of us?
3If you were completely sinless,
that would still mean nothing
to God All-Powerful.
4Is he correcting you
for worshiping him?
5No! It's because of
your terrible and endless sins.
6To guarantee payment of a debt,
you have taken clothes
from innocent people.
7And you refused bread and water
to the hungry and thirsty,
8although you were rich,
respected, and powerful.
9You have turned away widows
and have broken the arms
of orphans.
10That's why you were suddenly
trapped by terror,
11blinded by darkness,
and drowned in a flood.
God Lives in the Heavens
12God lives in the heavens
above the highest stars,
where he sees everything.
13Do you think the deep darkness
hides you from God?
14Do thick clouds cover his eyes,
as he walks around heaven's dome
high above the earth?
15Give up those ancient ideas
believed by sinners,
16who were swept away
without warning.
17They rejected God All-Powerful,
feeling he was helpless,
18although he had been kind
to their families.
The beliefs of these sinners
are truly disgusting.
19When God's people see
the godless swept away,
they celebrate, 20saying,
“Our enemies are gone,
and fire has destroyed
their possessions.”
Surrender to God All-Powerful
21Surrender to God All-Powerful!
You will find peace
and prosperity.
22Listen to his teachings
and take them to heart.
23If you return to God
and turn from sin,
all will go well for you.
24So get rid of your finest gold,
as though it were sand.
25Let God All-Powerful
be your silver and gold,
26and you will find happiness
by worshiping him.
27God will answer your prayers,
and you will keep the promises
you made to him.
28He will do whatever you ask,
and life will be bright.
29When others are disgraced,
God will clear their names
in answer to your prayers.
30Even those who are guilty
will be forgiven,
because you obey God.
translation_text:
Elifase noa dwirɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nza
1Temanniɛ Elifase buale kyɛ,
2 “Aso dasaniɛ nwo kɔhora konya mvasoɛ kɔma Nyameɛ anaa?
Nworɛniɛ po, aso ye nwo le mvasoɛ ma ye anaa?
3Sɛ ɛtengyɛ a, ɔfa Tuminiɛ ne nwo nzu,
yeɛ sɛ ngekalewa nne wɔ bra nu a, nzikyɛ mvasoɛ yeɛ onya ye ɔ?
4Ɛnwa nzɛ wɔ bra te sannwuu ti yeɛ ɔtwi wɔ nyunu ɔ,
bɔ ɔmaa obua wɔ ndɛen e?
5Aso nna wɔ bɔne bɔ ɔte piri ti ɔ?
W’amumuyɛɛ ne, ɔtra so.
6Ofikyɛ ama eliɛma mɔ bafa bɛ nningyein basi wɔ berɛ awowaa mbaen,
na apa bɛ nwo tena ama bɛ nwo ala so.
7Sona bɔ wayɛ bɛtɛɛ ne, amma ye nzue,
yeɛ bɔ ɛhɔen ku ye ne koso, afa aleɛ abɔ ye aheɛ.
8Sona bɔ tumi wura ye sa ne, wale aseɛ wabɔ so,
na bɔ tuminiɛ ne kuro ye dwirɛ ne yeɛ ɔtena so ɔ.
9Ama akunafoɛ mmrasua bele nzanza basa bahɔ,
na asisi awisiafoɛ.
10Ɔnate sɔ ati, ngaen mɔ apɛ wɔ nwo ayia,
mvum nu asane nwo ahunundetelɛ atɔ wɔ so.
11Awosii asi wɔ nye bɔ ennwu nikye ɔ,
na nzue ayi afa wɔ nwo nekaa biala.
12“Aso nna nyameɛso anwuro anwuro yeɛ Nyameɛ wɔ ɔ?
To wɔ nye nea anwuro anwuro nzramaa mɔ,
ná nwu kyɛbɔ besi bɛwɔ dededede ɔ!
13Nakoso ɛnwa: ‘Nyameɛ ɔse nzu?
Awosii kabii ye, aso okonwu yɛ kobua yɛ ndɛen?
14Munungum kabii amundu ye nwo, bɔ ɔmma onnwu nikye ɔ,
na ɔnate anwuro kango ne aso.
15Tete atennaa bɔ amumuyɛɛfoɛ bɛfale so ne,
so yeɛ ɛkɔfa hɔ anaa?
16Wandwu bɛ wue yeɛ ɔpraprale bɛ hɔle maa bewuwuli ɔ,
na nzueyilɛ piane bɛ nyinasoɛ hɔle.
17Na besele Nyameɛ kyɛ, ‘‘Fi yɛ so kɔ!
Nzikyɛ yeɛ Tuminiɛ ne kɔhora kɔfa kɔyɛ yɛ ɔ?’
18Nakoso ye yeɛ wafa nningyein paa wayi b’awuro tɛkyɛɛ ɔ,
na me de, mekyi bɔnefoɛ bɛ foɛtulɛ kɔkɔkɔkɔ.
19Bɛ bɔ bɛtengyɛ ne, benwu ye, na bɛ nye gye,
na bɛ bɔ bedi be ne goro bɛ nwo bɛka kyɛ,
20‘Amba, yɛ pɔfoɛ mɔ bɛ boso anua,
na agyapadeɛ bɔ bayakyi ye berɛ ne, see ayera ye.’
21“Odi kyɛ ɛne Nyameɛ bɛbɔ nu, ná ɛne ye bɛtena asomdwee nu,
na ɛyɔ sɔ a yeɛ okoyie wɔ yé ɔ.
22Di ye noa dwirɛ so,
ná fa ye dwirɛ sie wɔ ti anu.
23Sɛ esa kɔ Tuminiɛ ne berɛ a,
ɔkɔmaa ekosa kɔpe wɔ daa nu;
sɛ etu bra fiɛ bo efi w’awuro kɔ dededede a,
24sɛ ebu sikaa kɔkorɛ kyɛ mvuture a,
ɔne Ofire sikaa kɔkorɛ kyɛ asue nu nyɔboseka,
25ná ɛfa Tuminiɛ ne ɛyɛ wɔ sikaa kɔkorɛ,
ɔne wɔ dwetɛ paa paa a,
26ye de ekonya anika wɔ Tuminiɛ ne anu,
ná ama wɔ nye so anea Nyameɛ.
27Ɛkɔfa wɔ dwirɛ kɔto ye nyunu, na okotie wɔ,
ná atua w’aboadeɛ.
28Bɔ ɛkɔfa kosie wɔ nye so biala, ɔkɔyɛ berɛ kɔma wɔ,
na kanea kɔta w’atee so.
29Sɛ ɔbrɛ ebiemɔ ase a, ɛnwa anwomasoɛ ti ɔ,
ofikyɛ ɔpepɛ de anwobrɛaseɛniɛ.
30Sɛ sona bɔ onni be po, okole ye a,
nzaade wɔ nwo bɔ ɔte ne, okogyina so kole wɔ.”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
Today I Complain Bitterly
1Job said:
2Today I complain bitterly,
because God has been cruel
and made me suffer.
3If I knew where to find God,
I would go there
4and argue my case.
5Then I would discover
what he wanted to say.
6Would he overwhelm me
with his greatness?
No! He would listen
7because I am innocent,
and he would say,
“I now set you free!”
8I cannot find God anywhere—
in front or back of me,
9to my left or my right.
God is always at work,
though I never see him.
10But he knows what I am doing,
and when he tests me,
I will be pure as gold.
* 11I have never refused to follow
any of his commands,
12and I have always treasured
his teachings.
13But he alone is God,
and who can oppose him?
God does as he pleases,
14and he will do exactly
what he intends with me.
* 15Merely the thought
of God All-Powerful
16makes me tremble with fear.
17God has covered me
with darkness,
but I refuse to be silent.
translation_text:
Yob ma Elifase mmuayɛɛ
1Yeɛ Yob buale kyɛ,
2“Ɛnɛ koso, me nye aboro yeɛ mebɔ somoɛ ɔ,
me penenɛ bɔ mepene ne asi ne po,
wasa wafa amaneɛ wato me so.
3Ao! Sɛ ahaa mese nekaa bɔ ɔwɔ hɔ a,
sɛ ngɔhora ngoodwu nekaa bɔ ɔwɔ hɔ a!
4Ahaa ngɔbɔ me nguro wɔ ye nyunu,
ná mahyirehyire me dwirɛ ne anu mahyire ye.
5Ahaa ngɔte ye mmuayɛɛ bɔ ɔkɔfa kɔma me ɔ,
ná mate bɔ ɔkɔha kohyire me ne abo.
6Ye tumi piri ne, so yeɛ okogyina ɔne me kɔbɔ nguro anaa?
Daabi, ɔkɔyɛ asoɛ kotie me dwirɛ deɛ.
7Berɛ de, sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ ne, ɔkora ne ye bɛbɔ nguro,
na me ndɛenbualɛniɛ ne, okobua me be afebɔɔ.
8“Tie, sɛ mekɔ me nyunu a, ɔnne berɛ,
yeɛ mekɔ me si koso a, mennwu ye.
9Sɛ ɔyɔ adwuma wɔ me bɛen so a, mennwu ye,
yeɛ sɛ mekɔ famaa so koso a, me nye mbɛ ye so.
10Nakoso ye de, ɔse atee bɔ mefa so ɔ,
na sɛ oso me nea a,
ngofi nu ngofite ma me nwo kɔyɛ hyɛmm kyɛ sikaa kɔkorɛ.
11Mafa ye gya boso atee so pɛpɛɛpɛ,
na mali ye dwirɛ so bɔ manni ye nwo makyebu ɔ.
12Ye mmeraa bɔ wahyɛ ne, mmmuli so,
na ye noa dwirɛ ne, ye nwo hia me maa mafa masie me ti anu.
13Ye de, ye adwene nzesã,
nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora maa ɔkɔkakyi ye adwene ɔ?
Bɔ okuro ne yeɛ ɔyɔ ɔ.
14Ofikyɛ, bɔ wahyehyɛ wato berɛ wama me ne, ɔkɔmaa ɔkɔwa nu,
na ole sɔ nhyehyɛleɛ ne pee wɔ ye ti anu.
15Yiti mesuro kyɛ ngogyina ye nyunu ɔ,
na sɛ medwene sɔ dwirɛ ne anwo a, né ye nwo suronyi atɔ me so.
16Nyameɛ ama me nwo ngaka anwati,
Tuminiɛ ne ama ɛserɛ aha me.
17Ofikyɛ mandu mammini wɔ awosii ne anu,
nakoso wafa awosii kabii wamundu me nyunu.

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Doesn't God Set a Time?
1Why doesn't God
set a time for court?
Why don't his people know
where he can be found?
2Sinners remove boundary markers
and take care of sheep
they have stolen.
3They cheat orphans and widows
by taking their donkeys
and oxen.
4The poor are trampled
and forced to hide
5in the desert,
where they and their children
must live like wild donkeys
and search for food.
6If they want grain or grapes,
they must go to the property
of these sinners.
7They sleep naked in the cold,
because they have no cover,
8and during a storm
their only shelters are caves
among the rocky cliffs.
9Children whose fathers have died
are taken from their mothers
as payment for a debt.
10Then they are forced to work
naked in the grain fields
because they have no clothes,
and they go hungry.
11They crush olives to make oil
and grapes to make wine—
but still they go thirsty.
12And along the city streets,
the wounded and dying cry out,
yet God does nothing.
Some Reject the Light
13Some rebel and refuse
to follow the light.
14Soon after sunset they murder
the poor and the needy,
and at night they steal.
15Others wait for the dark,
thinking they won't be seen
if they sleep with the wife
or husband of someone else.
16Robbers hide during the day,
then break in after dark
because they reject the light.
17They prefer night to day,
since the terrors of the night
are their friends.
Sinners Are Filthy Foam
18Those sinners are filthy foam
on the surface of the water.
And so, their fields and vineyards
will fall under a curse
and won't produce.
19Just as the heat of summer
swallows the snow,
the world of the dead
swallows those who sin.
20Forgotten here on earth,
and with their power broken,
they taste sweet to worms.
21Sinners take advantage of widows
and other helpless women.
22But God's mighty strength
destroys those in power.
Even if they seem successful,
they are doomed to fail.
23God may let them feel secure,
but they are never
out of his sight.
24Great for a while; gone forever!
Sinners are mowed down
like weeds,
then they wither and die.
25If I haven't spoken the truth,
then prove me wrong.
translation_text:
Nzu ɔ Nyameɛ ndea bɔnefoɛ ndɛ ɔ?
1“Tuminiɛ ne, nzu ati yeɛ ondu mmerɛ bie nzie berɛ mva mmua bɔnefoɛ mɔ ndɛen ɔ?
Bɛ bɔ bedi ye dwirɛ so ne, nzu ati yeɛ bennwu ye ndɛenbualɛ mmerɛ ne ɔ?
2Bɔnefoɛ mɔ pimbi ɛwɛen,
bewua nyɛmmoa besie bɛ bɛfa.
3Bɛkye awisiafoɛ b’afunum mɔ bɛkɔ,
bede akunafoɛ mmrasua bɛ nandwie nyii bɛfa besi awowaa.
4Besumu mmenia bɔ bɛyɛ anwumvo ɔ befi atee so,
na aseɛ so ehiafoɛ amukoraa bɛbɔ nu bɛkɔfea.
5Na kyɛbɔ eburo afunum ɔyɔ ne,
sɔ ala yeɛ ehiafoɛ dwɔso kɔyɔ adwuma ɔ,
bɛpɛ aleɛ bɛkɔpena bɛ noa aleɛ,
na ɛserɛ so yeɛ bɛkɔtweetwee bɛpena aleɛ bɛma bɛ mma ɔ.
6Bɛpɛ ngaka aleɛ wɔ eburo,
na bɔnefoɛ fieso aleɛ bɔ bafa ne,
ye si bɔ waha berɛ ne yeɛ ehiafoɛ bɛsesa ɔ.
7Kɔngɔen bɛda kwaterekwa bɔ bennya ɛtena ɔ,
na ɛyerɛ ku bɛ a, bennya nikyee fee mva ngurɔ bɛ nwo.
8Mmokaa so esue bo bɛ ma bɛ nwo doa,
na bennya nekaa bɛmvea ne ati, bɛte bɛmata nyɔbotaen.
9“Bɔnefoɛ mɔ bɛte adɔma awisianiɛ befi nyɔfone noa,
na bɛfa ye besi oni ehianiɛ kerɛ nu awowaa.
10Ehiafoɛ natenate bɔ bɛ nwo la so ɔ, ofikyɛ belle ɛtena,
na bɛ kunu hɔen yeɛ bɛfa bɛsoa ebiemɔ aburoo bɔ babu ɔ.
11Ehiafoɛ betwi ngoo wɔ nyɔboɛ nyɔ b’afia,
betwi bobe mmaa nu bɛyɔ nzaa, nakoso nzuhɔen ku bɛ.
12Mmenia bɔ bɛla awusu ne, yɛte bɛ penelɛ ne nga wɔ kuro piri ne aso,
na bɛ bɔ bapira ne, bɛ kra bɔ awuye bɛpena mmokalɛ,
nakoso Nyameɛ ndɛ bɛ so.
13“Bɛte mmenia bɔ bedwɔso betia kanea ne,
bɛnze ye nwo atee ne,
yeɛ bɛmva ye atimbire ne aso.
14Wudiniɛ dwɔso alebahyene,
kyɛ ɔkwaahu sona bɔ ɔyɛ anwumvo ɔ, ɔne ehianiɛ,
na odwu kɔngɔen a, ɔte kyɛ awueniɛ.
15Bienzua bɔ ɔsɛkye agyaa ne, ɔnwondɛ kyɛ aleɛ kɔsa ɔ,
ɔka kyɛ, ‘Ebiala nye ngɔpɛ me so’,
na ɔfa nikyee kata ye nyunu.
16Awosii ba a, otofi sua terɛ nu tokuro,
aleɛ kye koso a, ɔto ye nwo anoa nu,
na ɔnze kyɛbɔ alehyeleɛ si te hyireinn ɔ.
17Sɔ mmenia ne amukoraa, awosii kabii yeɛ ɔte bɛ ngyerɛmɔ ɔ,
na bɛfa awosii kabii nu nningyein suronyisuronyi abiɛngoɛ.
18“Otu mini kyɛ ahure bɔ ɔwɔ nzue nye so ɔ,
ye aseɛ bɔ ole ye wɔ aseɛ ye aso ne, banoma ye,
na sona biala ngɔ ye bobe boo nu.
19Na kyɛbɔ wawa ne ahuhuro ma asukɔtwea nzue huro ne,
sɔ ala yeɛ ɛborɔ dɔ ma bɔnefoɛ betu bemini ɔ.
20Koɛsɛen bɔ ɔwole ye ne, ye wora fi ye,
ɔkakyi nnɔboakoma mɔ b’aleɛ,
mmenia ngaye ye ko,
na sɔ yeɛ amumuyɛɛ nu bubu kyɛ bakaa ɔ.
21“Brasua mmotaen bɔ ɔnnwo ɔ po, osisi ye,
na onnwu brasua kunaniɛ anwumvoin.
22Nakoso Nyameɛ nate ye tumi so ɔma tumifoɛ ngoa tendenn,
ɔwɔ nu kyɛ bɛ bo tindim de, nakoso belle anyelasoɛ.
23Ɔbɔ bɛ nwo waen ogyina bɛ si,
nakoso ye nye li b’atee bɔ bɛnate so ɔ si.
24Benya ngɔsoɛ, nakoso ɔngyɛ né bɛnne berɛ ko,
bɛkese, na betwindwam kyɛ ngyɛngyɛma,
na bɛpɛ bɛ begua kyɛ aburoo.
25Sɛ nna sɔ yeɛ ɔte hɔ a,
nwa yeɛ ɔkɔhora kɔha kyɛ nde ngondomboniɛ ɔ,
bɔ ɔkɔhora kohyire kyɛ nahorɛ nne me dwirɛ ne anu ɔ?”

english_text:
Bildad's Third Speech
God Is the One To Fear
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2God is the one to fear,
because God is in control
and rules the heavens.
3Who can count his army of stars?
Isn't God the source of light?
4How can anyone be innocent
in the sight of God?
5To him, not even the light
of the moon and stars
can ever be pure.
6So how can we humans,
when we are merely worms?
translation_text:
Bildade noa dwirɛ bɔ ɔtɔ so nza
1Yeɛ Suhiniɛ Bildade buale kyɛ,
2“Nyameɛ yeɛ ole tumi ná ye nwo yɛ suro ɔ,
ɔhyehyɛ asomdwee wɔ ye nyameɛso anwuro anwuro.
3Ye lɔen ne, aso ɛka bɛ a ekonwu ye noa?
Nwa yeɛ Nyameɛ kanea nda ye so ɔ?
4Nzaade ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né dasaniɛ watengyɛ wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu?
Sona bɔ brasua awo ye ɔ, ɔkɔyɛ sɛɛ né ye nwo ate?
5Sɛ ɛsraen po ɔnda hyireinn wɔ ye nye so,
yeɛ nzramaa mɔ po bɛ nwo nde wɔ ye nyunu a,
6né nzaade dasaniɛ bɔ ɔte nnɔboakoma ɔ,
kuro sona bɔ ɔte esuronyi ɔ, ogyi ye sɛ!”

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
You Have Really Been Helpful
1Job said:
2You have really been helpful
to someone weak and weary.
3You have given great advice
and wonderful wisdom
to someone truly in need.
4How can anyone possibly speak
with such understanding?
5Remember the terrible trembling
of those in the world of the dead
below the mighty ocean.
6Nothing in that land
of death and destruction
is hidden from God,
7who hung the northern sky
and suspended the earth
on empty space.
8God stores water in clouds,
but they don't burst,
9and he wraps them around
the face of the moon.
10On the surface of the ocean,
God has drawn a boundary line
between light and darkness.
11And columns supporting the sky
tremble at his command.
12By his power and wisdom,
God conquered the force
of the mighty ocean.
13The heavens became bright
when he breathed,
and the escaping sea monster
died at his hands.
14These things are merely a whisper
of God's power at work.
How little we would understand
if this whisper
ever turned into thunder!
translation_text:
Yob ma Bildade mmuayɛɛ
1Yeɛ Yob buale kyɛ,
2“Sona bɔ ɔyɛ mmerɛ ne, mmokalɛ bɔ afa ama ye hɔ ɛne!
Sona bɔ ye anwoserɛ ayie ne, mmokalɛ bɔ afa ama ye hɔ ɛne!
3Sona bɔ ɔnze nworɛ ne, foɛ bɔ atu ye hɔ ɛne!
Eh! Foɛ paa pee bɔ afa ama ye hɔ ɛne!
4Nwa yeɛ aha sɔ dwirɛ ne ahyire ye ne?
Nwa sunzum yeɛ ɔfa wɔ nu dwudwo ye?
5Awufoɛ mɔ bɛ nwo wosowoso bɛ wɔ aseɛ bo dɔ,
asue mɔ ne bɛ nu nningyein koso sɔ ala.
6Ɛborɔ nwo la so wɔ Nyameɛ nyunu,
yeɛ Abadɔn koso, ngatasoɛ biala nne so.
7Nyameɛ yeɛ ɔtrɛ sorɔ dɔ ewienu maa okodwu nekaa bɔ ɛhwee nne berɛ ɔ,
na ɔma aseɛ sinze berɛ bɔ nikyee fee nzosɔ nu ɔ.
8Ɔbɔ esue nonongu wura ye munungum nu,
nakoso nu nonɛ ne, ɔmma munungum ne anu nzua.
9Ɔkata ye ahennie bia ne nyunu,
na ɔtrɛtrɛ ye munungum nu fa kata so.
10Wafa ɛwɛen wato nzue anye,
na berɛ yeɛ ɔte kanea ne awosii b’ayieleɛ ɔ.
11Anwuro dɔ nyinasoɛ mɔ wosowoso,
na sɛ otwi bɛ nyunu a, bɛ nwo dwiri bɛ.
12Ɔfale ye tumi brɛle ɛpo ase,
na ɔfale ye nimdeɛ lili ɛpo nu sasrabɔnzam so ngonim.
13Ɔfale ye nwomeɛ mane ewienu tele kaenn,
yeɛ ɔfale ye sa sinane ewoo bɔ ɔnwati ne.
14Tie, bɔ Nyameɛ tumi kora yɔ ne, sɔ nningyein nemɔ te nu mmaa mmaa bie,
na kaaba bie yeɛ yate yafa Nyameɛ nwo ɔ.
Ye tumi totohyia ne, nwa yeɛ ɔkɔte ye bo ɔ?”

english_text:
Job Continues
I Am Desperate
1Job said:
2I am desperate because
God All-Powerful refuses
to do what is right.
As surely as God lives,
3and while he gives me breath,
4I will tell only the truth.
5Until the day I die,
I will refuse to do wrong
by saying you are right,
6because each day my conscience
agrees that I am innocent.
7I pray that my enemies
will suffer no less
than the wicked.
8Such people are hopeless,
and God All-Powerful
will cut them down,
9without listening
when they beg for mercy.
10And that is what God should do,
because they don't like him
or ever pray.
11Now I will explain in detail
what God All-Powerful does.
12All of you have seen these things
for yourselves.
So you have no excuse.
How God Treats the Wicked
13Here is how God All-Powerful
treats those who are wicked
and brutal.
14They may have many children,
but most of them will go hungry
or suffer a violent death.
15Others will die of disease,
and their widows
won't be able to weep.
16The wicked may collect riches
and clothes in abundance
as easily as clay.
17But God's people will wear
clothes taken from them
and divide up their riches.
18No homes built by the wicked
will outlast a cocoon
or a shack.
19Those sinners may go to bed rich,
but they will wake up poor.
20Terror will strike at night
like a flood or a storm.
21Then a scorching wind
will sweep them away
22without showing mercy,
as they try to escape.
23At last, the wind will celebrate
because they are gone.
translation_text:
Yob nwa odi be
1Yob toale so dwudwole kyɛ,
2“Nyameɛ bɔ ɔne me anni ye yé,
Tuminiɛ ne bɔ wama me kra odi aworabɔlɛ ne,
kyɛ ɔte ase ye de,
3kyɛbɔ ndɛ te ngoa nu ye,
bɔ Nyameɛ nwomeɛ tɛwɔ me nu ye de,
4me noa ngɔpɛ ngondombo,
yeɛ me temverema ngɔhã nnakannaka dwirɛ.
5Nyameɛ pa gua kyɛ ngɔhã kyɛ ɛmɔdi be ɔ,
na me nahorɛlilɛ de, mengɔyakyi nu kɔpem kyɛ ngowu ɔ.
6Ngotira me tenenee nu pindinn bɔ mengɔyakyi nu ɔ,
na me ngoa nu bɔ nde ye, me tiboa mmua me fɔ.
7“Mesrɛ kyɛ oyie me pɔfoɛ kyɛbɔ oyie amumuyɛɛniɛ ɔ,
ná oyie bɔ ɔko tia me ne kyɛbɔ oyie sona bɔ ɔndengyɛ ɔ.
8Sona bɔ ɔnze Nyameɛ ne, sɛ Nyameɛ pɛ ye ngoa so a,
sɛ ode ye ngoa fi ye sa nu a, ye anyelasoɛ wɔ ni?
9Sɛ edwirɛ to ye a,
aso Nyameɛ kotie ye sufrɛ?
10Aso ole anigye wɔ Tuminiɛ ne anu?
Aso osũ frɛ Nyameɛ mmerɛ biala anaa?
11Ngohyirehyire ɛmɔ Nyameɛ tumi ne nwo dwirɛ,
na Tuminiɛ ne, mengɔfa ye atee mengɔfea ɛmɔ.
12Na ɛmɔ amukoraa, sɛ ɛmɔ bɔbɔ ɛmɔanwu ye a,
nzu ati yeɛ ɛmɔkekã sɔ dwirɛ mbaen mbaen he ɔ?
13“Sona bɔ ɔte bɔnefoɛ ne, akatuaa bɔ onya fi Nyameɛ berɛ ɛhe,
yeɛ sona bɔ ɔhyɛ mmenia so koso, ye kyɛfa bɔ onya fi Tuminiɛ ne berɛ ɛhe:
14Sɛ ye mma mɔ bɛsone bɛyɛ pee a, ngrandɛ noa yeɛ bɛtotɔ ɔ,
yeɛ ye bosofoɛ ngonya aleɛ ngoli ngɔma bɛ ko ngoyi.
15Ye bosofoɛ bɔ bɛkɔha ne, ewue anwonyerɛ kohũ bɛ,
na ye kunafoɛ mmrasua ngosu.
16Ɔboaboa ɛdwetɛ noa kyɛ mvuture,
yeɛ ɔsoa ɛtena bɔ so kyɛ nnɛterɛ;
17ɔsoa bɔ so de, nakoso sona bɔ ɔtengyɛ yeɛ ɔkɔhera ɔ,
sona bɔ odi be yeɛ ɛdwetɛ ne kooli ye sa ɔ.
18Osi ye sua a, nu yɛ mmerɛ kyɛ mvrɔlɔ,
ɔte kyɛ asese bɔ wɛmvoɛ wasi ɔ.
19Sikaniɛ fa anwonya kɔda,
nakoso ye ayieleɛ ala ɛne,
sɛ ye nye te a, ye anwonya ne ɔnne berɛ ko.
20Ahunundetelɛ kakyi kyɛ asue oyi fa ye,
na mvrama bɔ ɔpɛ ye nwo ɔ fa ye kɔ kɔngɔen.
21Eyia afiteleɛ mvrama pagya ye kɔ,
na ɔpra ye fi ye awuro kɔ.
22Ɔbɔ ye kɔ bɔ onnwu ye anwumvoin ɔ,
na otu amirika serɛserɛ kyɛ ɔnwati fi ye sa nu.
23Ɔbɔ ye sa nu gua ye so,
na onwunanwuna ye wɔ nekaa biala bɔ ɔkɔ ɔ.

english_text:
Job Continues
Gold and Silver Are Mined
1Gold and silver are mined,
then purified;
2the same is done
with iron and copper.
3Miners carry lanterns
deep into the darkness
to search for these metals.
4They dig tunnels
in distant, unknown places,
where they dangle by ropes.
5Far beneath the grain fields,
fires are built
to break loose those rocks
6that have jewels or gold.
7Miners go to places unseen
by the eyes of hawks;
8they walk on soil unknown
to the proudest lions.
9With their own hands
they remove sharp rocks
and uproot mountains.
10They dig through the rocks
in search of jewels
